title: Vice President addresses Silver Jubilee celebrations of Balagokulam Delhi-NCR in New Delhi

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Silver Jubilee celebrations of Balagokulam Delhi-NCR:

I. The event was inaugurated by the President of India.
II. The celebration took place at the Thyagaraj Stadium in New Delhi.
III. The occasion marked 25 years of the organization's vision and impact.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.text: II and III only
answerOptions.rationale: The event was inaugurated by Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, not the President, while the location and the 25-year milestone are accurate.

answerOptions.text: I and II only
answerOptions.rationale: The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, was the chief guest and inaugural speaker, making statement I incorrect.

answerOptions.text: I and III only
answerOptions.rationale: While the Silver Jubilee signifies 25 years, the inauguration was performed by the Vice President, not the President.

answerOptions.text: I, II, and III
answerOptions.rationale: This option is incorrect because statement I wrongly attributes the inauguration to the President instead of the Vice President.

questions.hint: Identify the specific high-ranking official mentioned as the chief guest in the text.

questions.question: In his address, Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasized the national vision of 'Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi'. What is the primary objective of this approach according to the discourse?

answerOptions.text: Balancing civilisational pride with modern aspirations and development
answerOptions.rationale: The text states this approach connects children to their roots (Virasat) while equipping them for a changing future (Vikas).

answerOptions.text: Prioritizing industrial growth over the preservation of cultural heritage
answerOptions.rationale: The slogan suggests a dual focus rather than prioritizing one over the other, specifically seeking to maintain cultural roots.

answerOptions.text: Replacing traditional education with purely technical and modern vocational skills
answerOptions.rationale: The speech advocates for nurturing value-driven citizens rooted in culture, not replacing traditions with technical skills.

answerOptions.text: A government scheme aimed exclusively at urban infrastructure in Delhi-NCR
answerOptions.rationale: While the event was in Delhi, 'Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi' is described as a broader national vision for the youth's character and the nation's progress.

questions.hint: Think about the literal translation of the Hindi terms in the context of growth and heritage.

questions.question: What does the concept of 'Krishnarpanam', as described during the Rajatha Jayanti celebrations, signify?

answerOptions.text: The dedication of one’s thoughts, actions, and talents to a higher purpose
answerOptions.rationale: The Vice President explained that this concept embodies the essence of selfless action and dharma as taught by Lord Krishna.

answerOptions.text: A financial grant provided by the Ministry of Minority Affairs to cultural groups
answerOptions.rationale: The text describes it as a 'sacred offering' and a spiritual/philosophical concept, not a financial grant.

answerOptions.text: A specific curriculum designed for primary schools in New Delhi
answerOptions.rationale: Krishnarpanam is referred to as a sacred offering and a philosophical embodiment of teachings rather than a formal school curriculum.

answerOptions.text: The inauguration of a new stadium named after Lord Krishna
answerOptions.rationale: The event was held at the Thyagaraj Stadium; Krishnarpanam is the name of the offering/celebration theme.

questions.hint: Consider the philosophical meaning of making an offering of one's self and deeds.

questions.question: Which of the following pairings correctly matches the dignitary present at the event with their respective portfolio as of April 2026?

answerOptions.text: Shri Shripad Naik — Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy
answerOptions.rationale: The source material explicitly identifies Shri Shripad Naik with the portfolios of Power and New & Renewable Energy.

answerOptions.text: Shri George Kurian — Union Minister of State for Power
answerOptions.rationale: Shri George Kurian is identified as the MoS for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, Dairying & Minority Affairs.

answerOptions.text: Shri PK Suresh — Union Minister of State for Minority Affairs
answerOptions.rationale: Shri PK Suresh is the President of Balagokulam Delhi-NCR, not a Union Minister.

answerOptions.text: Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan — President of Balagokulam Delhi-NCR
answerOptions.rationale: Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan is the Vice President of India.

questions.hint: Recall the specific ministerial roles listed at the end of the press release.

questions.question: According to the Vice President, how does the vision of 'Amrit Kaal' relate to the citizens of India?

answerOptions.text: It calls for nurturing responsible, value-driven citizens to lead the nation
answerOptions.rationale: The text links the concept of Amrit Kaal to the development of citizens capable of leading the nation toward a prosperous future.

answerOptions.text: It focuses solely on increasing the per capita income of the youth
answerOptions.rationale: While prosperity is mentioned, the emphasis is specifically on values, character, and responsibility.

answerOptions.text: It refers to the transition from manual labor to automated industrial systems
answerOptions.rationale: The speech frames Amrit Kaal in terms of human character and civilizational pride rather than industrial automation.

answerOptions.text: It is a strategy to increase the visitor count of national stadiums
answerOptions.rationale: Amrit Kaal is presented as a broad vision for the nation's future and its people, not a local tourism or stadium strategy.

questions.hint: Look for the human-centric and character-driven aspects of the national vision.

questions.question: Regarding the role of children in Balagokulam, the Vice President described them as:

answerOptions.text: The true torch-bearers of the organization’s legacy
answerOptions.rationale: The text explicitly uses this phrase to describe the children being addressed at the event.

answerOptions.text: The primary administrators of the Silver Jubilee celebrations
answerOptions.rationale: The administrators include figures like Shri PK Suresh; children are described as the beneficiaries and legacy holders.

answerOptions.text: Recipients of the Rajatha Jayanti bravery awards
answerOptions.rationale: While they are celebrated, the text does not mention specific 'bravery awards' being given during the address.

answerOptions.text: Future candidates for the Union Ministry portfolios
answerOptions.rationale: Although they are described as future leaders, the specific phrase 'torch-bearers of the organization's legacy' is what was used.

questions.hint: Think of a metaphor involving fire or light used to describe passing on a tradition.

questions.question: Based on the Vice President's remarks, which qualities are specifically mentioned as necessary for children to imbibe to face future distractions and dilemmas?

answerOptions.text: Respect for elders, teamwork, and self-discipline
answerOptions.rationale: These specific values are listed as guidance for children to maintain clarity and confidence throughout their lives.

answerOptions.text: Competitive aggression and individual achievement
answerOptions.rationale: The speech emphasizes teamwork and cultural love rather than individualistic competition.

answerOptions.text: Technological proficiency and social media management
answerOptions.rationale: The VP views technology and changes as 'distractions' and suggests traditional values as the counter-balance.

answerOptions.text: Political activism and legislative knowledge
answerOptions.rationale: The focus of the speech is on character-building and culture rather than direct political training.

questions.hint: Review the section of the speech where the Vice President directly addresses the children.

questions.question: The Vice President noted that Lord Krishna’s life serves as an exemplar of which two principles?

answerOptions.text: Dharma and selfless action
answerOptions.rationale: The text explicitly states that Lord Krishna's life exemplifies dharma and selfless action for the greater good.

answerOptions.text: Economic reform and territorial expansion
answerOptions.rationale: These are modern political concepts not mentioned in the Vice President's description of Krishna's life.

answerOptions.text: Asceticism and total withdrawal from society
answerOptions.rationale: Krishna's teachings are associated with action and dharma within society, not isolation.

answerOptions.text: Technological innovation and maritime trade
answerOptions.rationale: These are unrelated to the spiritual and ethical principles highlighted in the speech.

questions.hint: Focus on the spiritual and ethical terms often associated with the Bhagavad Gita's philosophy.

questions.question: True or False: The Silver Jubilee celebrations of Balagokulam Delhi-NCR were held on April 18, 2026.

answerOptions.text: True
answerOptions.rationale: The PIB release date and the text within the report confirm the event occurred on April 18, 2026.

answerOptions.text: False
answerOptions.rationale: The date provided in the header and the body of the press release is specifically April 18, 2026.

questions.hint: Check the timestamp and the opening paragraph of the release.

questions.question: Which challenge of the contemporary world did the Vice President identify as something institutions like Balagokulam help mitigate for children?

answerOptions.text: Value-based dilemmas and numerous distractions
answerOptions.rationale: The speech notes that in a rapidly changing world, children face these specific issues, and Balagokulam acts as a guiding light.

answerOptions.text: Lack of access to digital infrastructure in urban areas
answerOptions.rationale: The text focuses on 'distractions'—implying an abundance of modern influence—rather than a lack of infrastructure.

answerOptions.text: The decline of the Silver Jubilee celebration tradition
answerOptions.rationale: The Silver Jubilee is being celebrated; it is not described as a contemporary challenge.

answerOptions.text: The shortage of stadiums for cultural confluence
answerOptions.rationale: The venue (Thyagaraj Stadium) is merely the setting; the challenge discussed is internal/moral growth.

questions.hint: Look for the specific internal conflicts children face in a 'rapidly changing world'.

content:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice President addresses Silver Jubilee celebrations of Balagokulam Delhi-NCR in New Delhi
Balagokulam is a confluence of culture and character, shaping generations of young minds: Vice-President
‘Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi’ must remain the guiding principle for the youth of the nation: Vice-President
'Amrit Kaal' vision calls for nurturing responsible, value-driven citizens
Posted On:
                        18 APR 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi
The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, addressed the inauguration of the Rajatha Jayanti (Silver Jubilee) celebrations of Balagokulam Delhi-NCR at Thyagaraj Stadium, INA, New Delhi, today.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the inauguration of the Silver Jubilee celebrations of Balagokulam Delhi-NCR at Thyagaraj Stadium, INA, New Delhi, today.
Marking 25 years of Balagokulam, the Vice President described the occasion as a celebration of a vision, a…
pic.twitter.com/Y059CE30im
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
April 18, 2026
Speaking about contemporary challenges, the Vice President noted that in a rapidly changing world, children face numerous distractions and value-based dilemmas. In this context, he emphasised that institutions like Balagokulam act as guiding lights, connecting children to their roots while equipping them to face the future with confidence and clarity. He said this approach reflects the national vision of “Vikas bhi, Virasat bhi.”
The Vice President underlined the importance of balancing civilisational pride with modern aspirations. He noted that the concept of Amrit Kaal calls for nurturing responsible and value-driven citizens capable of leading the nation towards a prosperous future.
Addressing the children, he described them as the true torch-bearers of the organisation’s legacy. He urged them to imbibe values such as respect for elders, love for culture, teamwork, and self-discipline, noting that these qualities would guide them throughout their lives.
On the occasion, he highlighted the significance of Krishnarpanam, being organised as a sacred offering during the Rajatha Jayanti celebrations. Explaining its deeper meaning, he said that dedicating one’s thoughts, actions, and talents to a higher purpose embodies the essence of Lord Krishna’s teachings. He noted that Lord Krishna’s life exemplifies dharma and selfless action for the greater good.
Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy,  Shri Shripad Naik; Union Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, Dairying & Minority Affairs, Shri George Kurian; President, Balagokulam Delhi-NCR, Shri PK Suresh and others were present during the occasion.
**********

(Release ID: 2253334)

title: Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan will undertake a two-day visit to Sri Lanka from April 19 to 20, 2026.

questions.question: Regarding the official visit of Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan to Sri Lanka in April 2026, which of the following statements is correct?

answerOptions.text: It marks the first bilateral visit by a Vice President of India to the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka.
answerOptions.rationale: The source explicitly identifies this two-day visit as the inaugural bilateral engagement by an Indian Vice President to the country.

answerOptions.text: It is the first visit by an Indian Head of State to Sri Lanka since the start of the housing project.
answerOptions.rationale: While significant, the Vice President is not the Head of State in India, and the text focuses on his specific office's first bilateral visit.

answerOptions.text: The visit marks the conclusion of all four phases of the Indian Housing Project.
answerOptions.rationale: Only the third phase is being marked as reaching a milestone, with a fourth phase still under construction.

answerOptions.text: The visit is exclusively focused on the diaspora in Colombo without regional travel.
answerOptions.rationale: The itinerary includes travel to Nuwara Eliya and interactions with leaders from the Northern and Eastern regions, showing a broader regional focus.

questions.hint: Consider the historical significance of the office holder's visit as mentioned in the introductory paragraph.

questions.question: The Vice President virtually handed over houses as part of the third phase of the Indian Housing Project. What is the cumulative total of houses built for Tamil communities with this completion?

answerOptions.text: 50,000 houses
answerOptions.rationale: The completion of the third phase brings the total number of houses provided to Tamil communities to this specific figure.

questions.question: On the second day of his visit, April 20, 2026, the Vice President's itinerary specifically includes travel to which location to visit housing projects?

answerOptions.text: Nuwara Eliya
answerOptions.rationale: The schedule specifically dictates a journey to this area on the second day for project inspection and community interaction.

answerOptions.text: Jaffna

answerOptions.text: Kandy
answerOptions.rationale: Kandy is a prominent city in Sri Lanka, but it is not listed as a destination in this specific bilateral itinerary.

answerOptions.text: Trincomalee

questions.hint: Look for the specific town mentioned in the latter half of the itinerary for April 20th.

questions.question: Which set of Sri Lankan leaders was the Vice President scheduled to meet on the first day of his visit?

answerOptions.text: President Anura Kumara Disanayaka and Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya
answerOptions.rationale: The release explicitly names these two current high-level officials as the primary dignitaries for the April 19 meetings.

answerOptions.text: President Ranil Wickremesinghe and Prime Minister Dinesh Gunawardena
answerOptions.rationale: These individuals represent previous holders of the offices and are not the dignitaries mentioned for this 2026 visit.

questions.hint: The names of the President and Prime Minister are provided in the second paragraph of the text.

questions.question: What is the primary diplomatic objective of this visit as stated in the context of recent high-level engagements?

answerOptions.text: To strengthen millennia-old civilizational and people-to-people ties between the two nations.
answerOptions.rationale: The concluding paragraph of the release highlights the reinforcement of these long-standing cultural and human connections.

answerOptions.text: To sign a new maritime boundary agreement in the Palk Strait.
answerOptions.rationale: The text focuses on community housing and civilizational ties rather than specific maritime boundary negotiations.

answerOptions.text: To establish a permanent military base in the Eastern region.
answerOptions.rationale: The visit focuses on housing projects and community engagement, not military expansion.

answerOptions.text: To initiate the first-ever trade agreement between India and Sri Lanka.
answerOptions.rationale: Trade relations are already established; this visit builds on existing 'millennia-old' ties rather than starting from zero.

questions.hint: Think about the historical and cultural depth of the relationship mentioned at the end of the text.

content:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan will undertake a two-day visit to Sri Lanka from April 19 to 20, 2026.
Posted On:
                        18 APR 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi
The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, will undertake an official visit to the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka from April 19 to 20, 2026. This will be the first bilateral visit by the Vice President of India to Sri Lanka.
During the visit, the Vice President will call on the President of Sri Lanka, H.E. Anura Kumara Disanayaka. He will also meet the Prime Minister of Sri Lanka, Dr. Harini Amarasuriya, along with other dignitaries on April 19, 2026.
He will interact with leaders of Indian-origin Tamil Community and Tamil Leaders from the Northern and Eastern regions of Sri Lanka.
Later in the day, the Vice President will address the Indian diaspora at a community event in Colombo, where he will virtually hand over houses to beneficiaries from Tamil communities,built with assistance from the Government of India as part of the third phase of the Indian Housing Project. With this, the total number of houses for Tamil communities will reach 50,000, and 10,000 more houses are being built in the fourth phase of the project.
On April 20, 2026, the Vice President will travel to Nuwara Eliya, visit the Indian Housing Projects, and interact with the local Tamil community.
This visit follows recent high-level engagements between the two countries and is expected to further strengthen the millennia-old civilizational and people-to-people ties between India and Sri Lanka.
*****
PR/ASM/VM
(Release ID: 2253231)

title: Prime Minister shares glimpses of his address to the Nation

questions.question:
Regarding the Prime Minister's address on the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, consider the following statements:
I. The opposition's resistance is described as an insult to the sentiments of the Constitution makers.
II. The Prime Minister characterized the amendment as a 'Mahayagya' intended to give 'new flight' to Indian women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

answerOptions.text: I only
answerOptions.rationale: While statement I is mentioned in the text, it is not the only correct statement, as the Prime Minister also explicitly used the term 'Mahayagya' for the amendment.

answerOptions.text: II only
answerOptions.rationale: While statement II accurately reflects the PM's metaphor for the amendment, statement I is also a primary claim made in the source material regarding the Constitution makers.

answerOptions.text: Both I and II
answerOptions.rationale: The source material confirms that the PM viewed the opposition as insulting the Constitution makers' sentiments and described the amendment as a 'Mahayagya' for women's empowerment.

answerOptions.text: Neither I nor II
answerOptions.rationale: Both statements are direct reflections of the Prime Minister's assertions regarding the legislative intent and the nature of the opposition's actions.

questions.hint: Consider the specific metaphors and historical references the Prime Minister used to justify the importance of the Act.

questions.question: Which of the following political parties were specifically cited by the Prime Minister as having 'committed foeticide' (bhroon-hatya) of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam amendment?

answerOptions.text: Congress, TMC, Samajwadi Party, and DMK
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister explicitly listed these four parties as the ones responsible for the metaphorical 'foeticide' of the amendment.

answerOptions.text: Congress, CPI(M), RJD, and AAP
answerOptions.rationale: While these are opposition entities, they were not the specific group of four parties listed in the PM's address provided in the text.

answerOptions.text: TMC, DMK, BRS, and Shiv Sena (UBT)
answerOptions.rationale: Only TMC and DMK from this list were specifically mentioned in the Prime Minister's series of posts regarding the amendment's rejection.

answerOptions.text: Samajwadi Party, BSP, JDS, and Congress
answerOptions.rationale: Though the Samajwadi Party and Congress are mentioned, the text does not include BSP or JDS in the specific list of parties accused of 'foeticide'.

questions.hint: Look for the specific list of regional and national parties mentioned in the second post.

questions.question: What primary psychological or political factor does the Prime Minister attribute to the 'Parivarvadi' (dynastic) parties' opposition to women's reservation?

answerOptions.text: A disagreement over the technical implementation of the quota
answerOptions.rationale: The text suggests the opposition is rooted in a fear of losing power rather than technical or administrative disagreements.

answerOptions.text: Fear that empowered women will threaten their existing leadership
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister explicitly states that dynastic parties fear that if women become empowered, their own leadership will be in danger.

answerOptions.text: Concerns regarding the constitutional validity of the amendment
answerOptions.rationale: The PM dismisses the opposition's motives as self-serving fear rather than legitimate legal or constitutional concerns.

answerOptions.text: A belief that the reservation percentage was insufficient
answerOptions.rationale: There is no mention in the text of the opposition wanting a higher percentage; instead, their motive is framed as a protection of dynastic interests.

questions.hint: Focus on the PM's critique of family-run political structures and their survival instincts.

questions.question: The Prime Minister expressed a personal hope that the Congress party would use the Women's Reservation Bill as an opportunity to do which of the following?

answerOptions.text: Propose a more comprehensive bill
answerOptions.rationale: The PM's focus was not on legislative improvements from the opposition but on a moral or historical correction.

answerOptions.text: Collaborate with regional parties for a consensus
answerOptions.rationale: The text emphasizes the Congress party's individual missed opportunity for internal atonement rather than coalition building.

answerOptions.text: Atone for their past 'sins' (paapon ka prayaschit)
answerOptions.rationale: The PM specifically mentions he hoped the Congress would use this opportunity for 'prayaschit' (atonement/penance) for past mistakes regarding women's reservation.

answerOptions.text: Demonstrate their commitment to secularism
answerOptions.rationale: The address specifically focuses on gender representation and 'Nari Shakti' rather than the principle of secularism.

questions.hint: Think of the religious or moral term used to describe making up for past errors.

questions.question: According to the Prime Minister's address, what is the predicted consequence for those who 'strike at the self-respect and self-esteem' of the nation's women?

answerOptions.text: They will face legal challenges in the Supreme Court
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister's warning is framed as a political and social reckoning from the people, not a specific legal process.

answerOptions.text: They will not be able to escape the wrath (akrosh) of mothers, sisters, and daughters
answerOptions.rationale: The text states that those hurting 'Nari Shakti' will not be able to avoid the anger or indignation of the women of the country.

answerOptions.text: They will be barred from participating in future 'Mahayagyas'
answerOptions.rationale: While 'Mahayagya' is a metaphor for the bill, the consequence for opposition is described in terms of the public outrage of women.

answerOptions.text: They will be forced to apologize to the Constitution makers
answerOptions.rationale: While their actions are called an insult to the founders, the consequence is specifically tied to the 'akrosh' (outrage) of the women themselves.

questions.hint: The PM uses a word describing a strong emotional response from the female population.

questions.question: In the context of the PM's statements, what does the term 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam' represent?

answerOptions.text: A new welfare scheme for maternal health
answerOptions.rationale: The context of the discussion is clearly centered on 'Mahila Arakshan' or Women's Reservation, not a health scheme.

answerOptions.text: A constitutional amendment regarding women's reservation
answerOptions.rationale: The text refers to it as an amendment related to women's reservation ('Mahila Arakshan') and a 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam'.

answerOptions.text: A judicial guideline for protecting women's dignity
answerOptions.rationale: The PM refers to it as an 'Adhiniyam' (Act/Bill) and an amendment, which implies a legislative rather than a judicial origin.

answerOptions.text: A policy for increasing women's participation in the labor force
answerOptions.rationale: The PM specifically focuses on the political empowerment and reservation aspect rather than economic labor policies.

questions.hint: Look for the Hindi term used alongside 'Arakshan' in the text.

questions.question: How does the Prime Minister describe the impact of the opposition's stance on the legacy of the Indian Constitution's architects?

answerOptions.text: As a fulfillment of the vision of the preamble
answerOptions.rationale: The PM argues the opposite, stating that the opposition's actions are a betrayal of the founders' vision.

answerOptions.text: As a necessary check and balance on executive power
answerOptions.rationale: The PM characterizes the opposition's role not as a democratic check, but as a derogatory act against the nation's founders.

answerOptions.text: As an insult to the sentiments of the Constitution makers
answerOptions.rationale: The text explicitly states that by opposing the reservation, the parties have 'insulted the feelings of the makers of the Constitution'.

answerOptions.text: As a move toward a more federal structure
answerOptions.rationale: The critique is focused on the betrayal of constitutional values regarding gender empowerment, not federalism.

questions.hint: The PM links the current legislative debate back to the original authors of India's foundational document.

questions.question: Which specific metaphor is used in the text to describe the act of blocking or opposing the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam amendment?

answerOptions.text: A hurdle in the path of progress
answerOptions.rationale: While logically true in the PM's view, the specific and more severe metaphor used is 'bhroon-hatya'.

answerOptions.text: Foeticide (Bhroon-hatya)
answerOptions.rationale: The PM used this specific, evocative term to describe how the Congress and other parties killed the amendment in its early stages.

answerOptions.text: A dark cloud over democracy
answerOptions.rationale: The PM's language is more specifically targeted at the 'life' of the amendment itself using biological metaphors.

answerOptions.text: An eclipse of the nation's pride
answerOptions.rationale: This is a plausible distractor, but the text specifically uses 'bhroon-hatya' to describe the opposition's impact on the amendment.

questions.hint: The PM uses a term typically associated with the termination of a life before birth.

questions.question: According to the Prime Minister, the 'new flight' (nai udaan) for the women of Bharatvarsh was intended to be facilitated through which mechanism?

answerOptions.text: Economic subsidies for women entrepreneurs
answerOptions.rationale: The 'flight' mentioned is specifically linked to the 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam' amendment, which concerns political reservation.

answerOptions.text: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam amendment
answerOptions.rationale: The PM states that the amendment was a 'Mahayagya' meant to give a 'new flight' to the women of India.

answerOptions.text: Educational quotas in premier institutions
answerOptions.rationale: The text focuses on the specific legislative amendment for reservation, not general educational quotas.

answerOptions.text: The dissolution of dynastic political parties
answerOptions.rationale: While the PM criticizes these parties, the 'flight' itself is provided by the Act/Amendment, not the removal of the parties.

questions.hint: Identify the legislative instrument the Prime Minister is defending in his posts.

questions.question: The PM's address suggests that opposition to women's reservation is not merely a political difference but a strike against which of the following?

answerOptions.text: International diplomatic standing
answerOptions.rationale: The address is focused on the internal socio-political fabric and the self-respect of Indian women, not foreign relations.

answerOptions.text: The economic stability of the middle class
answerOptions.rationale: The PM focuses on the dignity and power of 'Nari Shakti' (women power) rather than economic indicators.

answerOptions.text: The self-respect and self-esteem of women power (Nari Shakti)
answerOptions.rationale: The text explicitly states that those who strike at the 'svabhiman' (self-respect) and 'atmasamman' (self-esteem) of women will face their wrath.

answerOptions.text: The legislative authority of the Parliament
answerOptions.rationale: The emphasis is on the personal and collective dignity of women as a social force rather than just a procedural insult to Parliament.

questions.hint: Look for the Hindi terms 'svabhiman' and 'atmasamman' and what they refer to in the text.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addresses the nation

questions.question: Regarding the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam Amendment, which of the following statements best reflects the Prime Minister's clarification on the delimitation process?

answerOptions.text: The amendment would lead to a reduction in seats for smaller states to accommodate larger ones.
answerOptions.rationale: The source material explicitly states that the government ensured no state would lose representation.

answerOptions.text: Every state would see a proportional and fair increase in parliamentary seats.
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister clarified that the government's plan ensured seat increases across all states in an equal and fair proportion.

answerOptions.text: Only states like Tamil Nadu and Bengal were slated for seat increases to address regional imbalances.
answerOptions.rationale: While these states were mentioned as examples of beneficiaries, the policy applied to all states, not just those listed.

answerOptions.text: The delimitation was postponed indefinitely due to opposition from dynastic parties.
answerOptions.rationale: The failure of the bill stalled the process, but the Prime Minister's clarification focused on the fairness of the intended seat distribution, not a planned postponement.

questions.hint: Consider the Prime Minister's response to narratives regarding how seats would be distributed among various states.

questions.question: According to the Prime Minister, why do 'dynastic parties' perceive the empowerment of women outside their families as a threat?

answerOptions.text: Because non-dynastic women prioritize national interests over regional party agendas.
answerOptions.rationale: While true in a broader sense, the Prime Minister specifically highlighted the threat to localized leadership structures.

answerOptions.text: Because they fear capable women in Panchayats will challenge their entrenched leadership.
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister noted that thousands of capable women serving in Panchayats pose a direct challenge to the security of dynastic politicians.

answerOptions.text: Because the amendment would mandate that 100 percent of leadership roles be held by women.
answerOptions.rationale: The source mentions '100 percent' in the context of women's blessings for the government, not a mandate for all leadership roles.

answerOptions.text: Because dynastic parties believe women are naturally inclined toward opposing digital reforms like GST.
answerOptions.rationale: The source suggests the opposite: that dynastic parties, not women, opposed digital reforms and the GST.

questions.question: The Prime Minister listed several 'national resolutions' that he claimed were stalled for 40 years. Which of the following was NOT explicitly mentioned in this context?

answerOptions.text: Settlement of long-standing border disputes.
answerOptions.rationale: Border dispute settlements were listed among the necessary decisions that were previously 'swept under the carpet'.

answerOptions.text: Reservations for Other Backward Classes (OBC).
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister included OBC reservations in the list of delayed decisions that caused generations to suffer.

answerOptions.text: The universal implementation of the Digital India initiative.

answerOptions.rationale: While the PM mentioned GST opposition, he did not link it to what women specifically 'never forget'.

answerOptions.rationale: The PM described delimitation claims as 'false narratives' used by the opposition, not something defining women's memory.

answerOptions.text: An insult to their pride and self-respect.
answerOptions.rationale: The PM stated, 'Women may forget everything, but will never forget insult to their pride'.

questions.question: The Prime Minister referred to the opposition's actions against the women's reservation as a 'sin'. What consequence did he predict for this?
questions.text: Which of the following describes the punishment the PM believes the opposition will face?

answerOptions.rationale: The PM used 'Mahayagya' to describe the amendment itself, not a future event the opposition would be barred from.

answerOptions.rationale: The PM stated that the opposition will be punished for the sin they have committed and that women will hold them strictly accountable.

content:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addresses the nation
Women may forget everything, but will never forget insult to their pride: PM
Those parties that have opposed the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam Amendment in Parliament are taking women's power for granted: PM
Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam Amendment  was a 'Mahayagya' to empower women of the 21st century : PM
One major reason for opposition to Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam by dynastic parties is their fear : PM
The blessings of the country's 100 percent Nari Shakti are with us: PM
We will remove every obstacle coming in the way of women's reservation: PM
Snatching away women's rights, these people were thumping the tables ; That was an assault on the dignity of women, on their self-respect: PM
For opposing women’s reservation, the opposition will be punished for the sin they have committed: PM
Posted On:
                        18 APR 2026 11:39PM by PIB Delhi
Addressing the nation on a highly critical issue concerning the mothers, sisters, and daughters of India, the Prime Minister expressed his profound sorrow over the stalling of women's progress. He noted that despite the government's utmost and sincere efforts, the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam Amendment failed to pass, effectively crushing the legitimate dreams of the female population. "I deeply apologize to all the mothers and sisters of the nation for this unfortunate outcome," stated Shri Modi.
Highlighting that the national interest remains strictly paramount, the Prime Minister sharply criticized specific political factions for prioritizing partisan gains over the welfare of the country.
Reflecting on the profound disappointment witnessed across the country, the Prime Minister pointed out that
defeat of this bill is a direct blow to the self-respect of women, an insult that the female electorate will permanently engrave in their memories. "Women may forget everything else, but they never forget an insult to their pride," affirmed Shri Modi.
The
Prime Minister highlighted that women of India are acutely aware of the malicious intentions and will hold the offending politicians strictly accountable in the future. Detailing the transformative vision of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam Amendment, the Prime Minister explained that the legislation was a grand effort designed to grant long-pending rights and create new opportunities for half the population. He observed that the bill aimed to remove systemic obstacles and equally amplify the political power of all states, regardless of their size or geography. "This amendment was a sincere effort to make women equal co-travelers in India's development journey," pointed out Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister emphasized that the citizens of India have thoroughly recognized this ugly pattern of politics and fully understand the underlying motives. "The country has now completely understood the ugly political pattern used to steal women's rights," affirmed Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister explained that dynastic parties are terrified that empowered women from outside their families will threaten their localized leadership. He highlighted that the thousands of capable women currently serving in Panchayats pose a direct challenge to the deeply entrenched insecurity of dynastic politicians.
Dismantling the  false narratives regarding delimitation, the Prime Minister clarified that the government had explicitly ensured no state would lose representation, as all states would see their seats increase in equal, fair proportion. Highlighting the missed opportunities for regional growth, the Prime Minister stated that the amendment would have significantly increased parliamentary seats for states like Tamil Nadu, Bengal, and Uttar Pradesh.
Listing a series of transformative initiatives opposed earlier, the Prime Minister pointed out that  the Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile trinity, digital payments, GST, and the law against Triple Talaq were also resisted. He highlighted that earlier chaos has also been created over the CAA law and efforts to eradicate Maoist violence have been constantly hindered.
Tracing India's historical developmental delays, the Prime Minister stated that the persistent strategy of sweeping necessary decisions under the carpet allowed other nations to surpass India post-independence. He highlighted that  40 years have been spent stalling crucial national resolutions, including border dispute settlements, OBC reservations, and the One Rank One Pension scheme for soldiers.
The Prime Minister noted that generations of Indians have suffered deeply due to such indecision and deceit. He emphasized that the current political battle is not just about a single piece of legislation, but a broader war against a deeply negative, anti-reform mentality. "I have no doubt that all the sisters and daughters of the country will give a fitting reply to this toxic mentality," pointed out Shri Modi.
Dismissing claims that the failure of the bill reflects poorly on the government, the Prime Minister reiterated that he was perfectly willing to give the opposition full credit through advertisements if they had simply supported the legislation. "This issue was never about taking political credit; it was about securing rights," asserted Shri Modi.
Reaffirming his unwavering commitment to women's empowerment, the Prime Minister expressed solidarity with the sadness felt by millions of women, assuring them that his resolve remains entirely unbroken despite the lack of parliamentary numbers. He promised to eliminate every future obstacle in the path of the legislation, declaring that the Government  will eventually succeed with the blessings of 100 percent of the nation's women. "For the dreams of half the population and the future of the country, we have to fulfill this resolution," emphasized Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM’s address to the Nation

questions.question:
Regarding the Nari Shakti Vandan amendment discussed in the text, consider the following statements:

1. It aimed to provide reservation for women starting from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
2. The amendment was intended to provide rights to $50\%$ of the country's population.
3. It required a simple majority of total membership in Parliament to pass.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.text: 1 and 2 only
answerOptions.rationale: The text specifies that the rights were pending for 40 years to be implemented from the 2029 elections for half the population, but it failed due to not meeting the required two-thirds ($66\%$) threshold.

answerOptions.text: 2 and 3 only
answerOptions.rationale: While the amendment targeted $50\%$ of the population, the text explicitly mentions that a $66\%$ vote was required, which is a special majority, not a simple majority.

answerOptions.text: 1 and 3 only
answerOptions.rationale: While the 2029 date is correct, the requirement for a $66\%$ vote indicates that a simple majority is insufficient for this type of constitutional amendment.
The third statement is incorrect because the Prime Minister noted that $66\%$ of the votes were required, signifying a special majority rather than a simple one.

questions.hint: Focus on the specific implementation year and the percentage of votes the Prime Minister mentioned as necessary for passing the bill.

questions.question: According to the Prime Minister's address, how would the delimitation process affect the representation of different states in Parliament?

answerOptions.text: The seats of all states would increase in equal proportion without changing the relative participation ratio.
answerOptions.rationale: The speech clarifies that the government intended for the seats in all states to increase equally so that no state's relative representation or participation would be reduced.

answerOptions.text: States with smaller populations would see a decrease in seats to balance larger states.
answerOptions.rationale: This reflects a common fear mentioned in the text that the government explicitly denied, stating that no state's representation would be reduced.

answerOptions.text: Only states in the North and West would see an increase in seat counts due to population growth.
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister emphasized that the effort was to increase the strength of every state across the North, South, East, and West equally.

answerOptions.text: The proportion of participation for larger states would be increased to reflect current demographic trends.
answerOptions.rationale: The text explicitly states that the proportion of participation for any state would not change, contradicting the idea of shifting proportions toward larger states.

questions.hint: Consider the government's assurance regarding the 'proportion of participation' and the geographical balance of the reform.

questions.question:
The text identifies several historical reforms and laws that the opposition parties supposedly obstructed. Which of the following were mentioned?

1. Goods and Services Tax (GST)
2. One Nation One Election
3. Removal of Article 370
4. Reforms in the Waqf Board

Select the correct answer using the code below:

answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister listed GST, One Nation One Election, Article 370, and Waqf Board reforms as specific examples of initiatives the Congress and its allies have opposed.

answerOptions.text: 1 and 3 only
answerOptions.rationale: While these are correct, the text also explicitly includes 'One Nation One Election' and 'Waqf Board reforms' in the list of obstructed items.

answerOptions.text: 1, 2, and 3 only
answerOptions.rationale: This option omits the Waqf Board reforms, which the Prime Minister specifically highlighted as a subject of opposition protest.

answerOptions.text: 2, 3, and 4 only
answerOptions.rationale: This option omits GST, which was explicitly mentioned in the text as a reform the Congress party opposed.

questions.hint: The Prime Minister provided a long list of varied reforms, ranging from taxation to constitutional status and administrative boards.

questions.question: What reason does the Prime Minister provide for the opposition of 'family-oriented' parties to the Nari Shakti Vandan amendment?

answerOptions.text: A fear that empowered women from outside their own families would threaten their political leadership.
answerOptions.rationale: The speech claims these parties feel insecure about women outside their families moving into the Lok Sabha and Assemblies, fearing a loss of leadership control.

answerOptions.text: Technical concerns regarding the structural implementation of women's reservations in Panchayats.
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister dismisses 'technical snags' as mere excuses and notes that women have already proven their capability in Panchayats.

answerOptions.text: The belief that women's reservation should only be implemented after a new census is completed.
answerOptions.rationale: The text characterizes opposition arguments as 'falsehoods' and 'excuses' rather than legitimate census-based concerns.

answerOptions.text: Concerns that the amendment would undermine the authority of regional party leaders in Tamil Nadu and Bengal.
answerOptions.rationale: While regional parties like DMK and TMC are mentioned, the primary motivation cited is the protection of 'family-oriented' leadership rather than regional authority.

questions.hint: Think about the personal stakes mentioned for leaders whose parties are dominated by specific lineages.

questions.question: With reference to the Prime Minister's critique of the Congress party's history, which delay was specifically noted as lasting for 40 years?

answerOptions.text: The decision on OBC reservation and One Rank One Pension.
answerOptions.rationale: The Prime Minister cited both the OBC reservation and One Rank One Pension (OROP) as specific examples of decisions delayed for four decades by previous administrations.

answerOptions.text: The implementation of the Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity.
answerOptions.rationale: JAM is described as a reform the Congress opposed during its rollout, but it is not cited as a 40-year delay.

answerOptions.text: The removal of Article 370 and the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code.
answerOptions.rationale: While these are mentioned as points of opposition, they were not grouped under the specific 40-year delay timeline in this speech.

answerOptions.text: The settlement of water-sharing disputes with Pakistan.
answerOptions.rationale: The text mentions that Congress 'delayed' water disputes, but it does not assign the specific '40 years' timeframe to this issue.

questions.hint: Look for the specific examples where the Prime Minister highlights a long-term neglect of soldiers and backward classes.

questions.question: The Prime Minister uses the term 'foeticide' in a metaphorical sense to describe what action in Parliament?

answerOptions.text: The obstruction and defeat of the Nari Shakti Vandan amendment by the opposition.
answerOptions.rationale: The speech uses this strong term to characterize the act of 'killing' the bill before it could be enacted, blaming Congress and its allies for this outcome.

answerOptions.text: The historical neglect of the girl child in rural Indian communities.
answerOptions.rationale: While the term 'foeticide' usually refers to this, in the context of this speech, it is explicitly used to describe the fate of the legislative proposal.

answerOptions.text: The reduction of women's representation in regional legislative assemblies.
answerOptions.rationale: The text focuses on the failure to pass the federal amendment rather than a pre-existing reduction in regional seats.

answerOptions.text: The suppression of internal democratic processes within family-led political parties.
answerOptions.rationale: The PM critiques family-led parties for being 'anti-women,' but the specific term 'foeticide' is applied to the death of the amendment bill.

questions.hint: Identify the specific 'honest effort' or 'proposal' that the PM claims was 'subjected to foeticide' in the halls of the legislature.

questions.question: Based on the text, what was the PM's offer to the opposition regarding the 'credit' for the bill?

answerOptions.text: He offered to publish advertisements featuring photos of opposition leaders if they supported the bill.
answerOptions.rationale: The PM stated he was willing to give all credit to the opposition, including publishing their photos in advertisements, if they allowed the bill to pass.

answerOptions.text: He proposed a joint parliamentary committee where the opposition would hold the chairmanship.
answerOptions.rationale: There is no mention of offering committee chairmanships or structural leadership roles to the opposition in the text.

answerOptions.text: He suggested that the bill be renamed to include the names of prominent opposition founders like Lohia.
answerOptions.rationale: The PM mentions that the SP 'trampled' Lohia's dreams, but he did not offer to rename the act after him.

answerOptions.text: He offered to delay the delimitation process if the opposition agreed to the reservation percentage.
answerOptions.rationale: The PM defended the delimitation process and did not offer to delay it; he focused on giving the opposition political credit instead.

questions.hint: Look for the section where the PM discusses whether the bill was about 'success or failure' and mentions advertisements.

questions.question: Which specific regional parties are accused by the Prime Minister of betraying the people of their own states (specifically Tamil Nadu and Bengal) by opposing the bill?

answerOptions.text: DMK and TMC

content:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM’s address to the Nation
Posted On:
                        18 APR 2026 9:48PM by PIB Delhi
Today I have come to speak on a very important subject, especially to the mothers, sisters, and daughters of the country! Today every citizen of India is watching how the flight of women power has been stopped. Their dreams have been ruthlessly crushed. Despite our utmost efforts, we could not succeed, the amendment to the Nari Shakti Vandan Act could not be passed! And for this, I seek forgiveness from all the mothers and sisters.
Friends,
For us, national interest is paramount, but when for some people party interest becomes everything, when party interest becomes bigger than national interest, then women power and national interest have to bear the consequences. This time too, the same has happened. The selfish politics of parties like Congress, DMK, TMC, and Samajwadi Party has harmed the women power of the country.
Friends,
Yesterday, the eyes of crores of women in the country were on Parliament, the women power of the nation was watching. I too felt very sad to see that when this proposal in favor of women fell, parties like Congress, DMK, TMC, and SP, family-oriented parties, were clapping with joy. By snatching away the rights of women, they were thumping the tables. What they did was not just thumping on the tables, it was a blow to the self-respect and dignity of women. And women forget everything, but they never forget their insult. Therefore, the pain of the behavior of Congress and its allies in Parliament will always remain in the hearts of women. Whenever the women of the country see these leaders in their areas, they will remember that it was these very people who celebrated in Parliament when women’s reservation was stopped, they rejoiced. To those parties who opposed the Nari Shakti Vandan amendment in Parliament yesterday, I will say clearly: these people are taking women power for granted. They are forgetting that the women of the 21st century are watching every event in the country, they are sensing their intentions, and they have fully understood the truth. Therefore, for opposing women’s reservation, the sin committed by the opposition will surely bring punishment to them. These parties have also insulted the sentiments of the framers of the Constitution, and they will not escape the punishment from the people either.
Friends,
The Nari Shakti Vandan amendment was not about taking anything away from anyone. The Nari Shakti Vandan amendment was about giving something to everyone, it was an amendment to give. It was about giving women the right that has been pending for 40 years, from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections onwards.
The Nari Shakti Vandan amendment was a great effort to give new opportunities, new flight, and to remove obstacles from the path of the women of 21st century India. It was a sacred effort made with clear intent and honesty to give rights to 50% of the country’s population. It was an effort to make women co-travelers in India’s journey of development and to include everyone. The Nari Shakti Vandan amendment is the demand of the time. The Nari Shakti Vandan amendment was an effort to equally increase the strength of every state, North, South, East, West. It was an effort to give more strength to the voice of every state in Parliament. Whether the state is small or big, whether the population is less or more, it was an effort to increase everyone’s strength in equal proportion. But this honest effort has been subjected to foeticide in Parliament by Congress and its allies, foeticide. Congress, TMC, Samajwadi Party, DMK—these parties are guilty of this foeticide. They are criminals against the Constitution of the country, they are criminals against the women power of the country.
Friends,
Congress hates the subject of women’s reservation, it has always conspired to stop women’s reservation. Every time efforts were made in this direction, Congress obstructed them. This time too, Congress and its allies relied on one falsehood after another to stop women’s reservation. Sometimes about numbers, sometimes in other ways, Congress and its allies tried to mislead the country. By doing so, these parties have revealed their true face before the women power of India. They have removed their mask.
Friends,
Personally, I had hoped that Congress would correct its decades-old mistake. Congress would repent for its sins. But Congress lost the opportunity to create history, to stand in favor of women. Congress has already lost its existence in most parts of the country. Congress is surviving like a parasite, riding on the back of regional parties. But Congress does not even want regional parties to grow stronger, so Congress conspired politically to push the future of many regional parties into darkness by making them oppose this amendment.
Friends,
Congress, Samajwadi Party, DMK, TMC, and other parties have, for so many years, every time created the same excuses, the same false arguments, always inserting some technical snag, and they have looted the rights of women. The country has understood this ugly pattern of politics, and it has also understood the reason behind it.
Brothers and sisters,
One big reason for the opposition to the Nari Shakti Vandan Act is the fear of these family-oriented parties. They fear that if women become empowered, then the leadership of these family-oriented parties will be in danger. They will never want women outside their families to move forward. Today, in Panchayats and local bodies, thousands and millions of women have proven their capability. When they want to move forward into Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies, when they want to serve the country, these family-oriented parties feel insecure. After delimitation, there will be many more seats for women, women’s stature will increase, and that is why these people opposed the Nari Shakti Vandan amendment. The women power of the country will never forgive Congress and its allies for this sin.
My dear countrymen,
Congress and its allied parties are continuously, continuously lying about delimitation. They want to ignite the fire of division under this pretext. Because “divide and rule” politics is something Congress inherited from the British. And Congress is still running on that same path today. Congress has always fueled sentiments that create rifts in the country. Therefore, this lie was spread that delimitation would harm some states! Whereas the government has made it clear from the very first day that neither the proportion of participation of any state will change, nor will anyone’s representation be reduced. In fact, the seats of all states will increase in equal proportion. Yet Congress, DMK, TMC, and Samajwadi Party were not ready to accept this.
Friends,
This amendment bill was an opportunity for all parties and all states. If this bill had passed, Tamil Nadu, Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala, every state’s seats would have increased. But because of their selfish politics, these parties betrayed even the people of their own states. For example, DMK had the chance to make more Tamil people MPs and MLAs, to strengthen Tamil Nadu’s voice! But it lost that chance. TMC also had the chance to advance the people of Bengal. But TMC too lost that chance. Samajwadi Party had the chance to reduce the stain of its anti-women image. But SP missed it too. SP has already forgotten Lohia ji. By opposing the Nari Shakti Vandan amendment, SP trampled all of Lohia ji’s dreams underfoot. SP is anti-women reservation, and the women of UP and the country will never forget this.
Friends,
By opposing women’s reservation, Congress has once again proved one thing. Congress is an anti-reform party. For a developed India in the 21st century, whatever decisions, whatever reforms are necessary, whatever decisions the country takes, Congress opposes them, rejects them, obstructs them. This is the history of Congress and this is Congress’s negative politics.
Friends,
This is the same Congress that opposed the trinity of Jan Dhan–Aadhaar–Mobile. Congress opposed digital payments. Congress opposed GST. Congress opposed reservation for the poor in the general category. Congress opposed the law against triple talaq. Congress opposed the removal of Article 370. Our Constitution, our courts, have said that the Uniform Civil Code, UCC, is necessary, but Congress opposes that too. At the very mention of reform, Congress runs with placards of protest. Any work that strengthens the country, Congress puts all its strength into creating obstacles in it. Congress opposes One Nation One Election. Congress opposes driving out infiltrators from the country. Congress opposes purification of the voter list, SIR. Congress opposes reforms in the Waqf Board.
Friends,
Congress even opposed the CAA law that gave security to refugees. By lying and spreading rumors, it created a storm in the country. Congress obstructs the country’s efforts to end Maoist–Naxalite violence. Congress has had only one pattern: whenever a reform comes, lie, spread confusion. History is witness, Congress has always chosen this negative path.
Friends,
Whatever decision is necessary for the country, Congress sweeps it under the carpet. Because of this attitude of Congress, India has not reached the heights of development it deserves. At the time of independence, many other countries were freed along with us. Most of those countries went far ahead of us, and the reason was that Congress kept blocking every reform. Delay, diversion, obstruction—this was Congress’s principle, this was Congress’s work culture. Congress delayed border disputes with neighboring countries. Congress delayed water-sharing disputes with Pakistan. Congress delayed the decision on OBC reservation for 40 years. Congress delayed One Rank One Pension for soldiers for 40 years.
Friends,
This attitude of Congress has always caused great harm to the country. The nation has suffered from every opposition, every indecision, every deceit of Congress. Generations of the country have suffered. Today, all the major challenges before the country have arisen from this attitude of Congress. Therefore, this fight is not just about one law, this fight is against Congress’s anti-reform mentality, which is filled only with negativity. And I have no doubt that the women and daughters of the country will give a strong reply to this mentality of Congress.
Friends,
Some people are calling the breaking of the dreams of the women of the country a failure of the government. But this subject was never about success or failure, never about credit. I had said in Parliament too: let half the population get their rights, I will give the credit to the opposition by publishing advertisements with all their photos. But those who look at women with outdated thinking still stuck to their lies, remained firm!
Friends,
The fight to give women power participation has been going on for decades. For years, I too have been among those making efforts for it. So many women have raised this subject before me. So many sisters have written letters to me explaining everything. My country’s mothers, sisters, daughters—I know you are all sad today. I too share in your sorrow. Today, even though we did not get the required 66 percent votes to pass the bill, I know that 100 percent of the women power of the country has blessed us. I assure every woman of the country: we will remove every obstacle in the path of women’s reservation. Our courage is high, our determination unbreakable, and our resolve unwavering. The parties opposing women’s reservation will never be able to stop the women power of this country from increasing their participation in Parliament and Legislative Assemblies. It is only a matter of time. The BJP–NDA’s resolve for the empowerment of women power is intact. Yesterday we did not have the numbers, but that does not mean we lost. Our inner strength is invincible. Our effort will not stop, our effort will not pause. We will have more opportunities ahead. For the dreams of half the population, for the future of the country, we must fulfill this resolve. Thank you all very much.
DISCLAIMER: This is the approximate translation of the PM's speech. The original speech was delivered in Hindi.
**********

SEVENTH SESSION OF EIGHTEENTH LOK SABHA CONCLUDES
Posted On:
                        18 APR 2026 3:22PM by PIB Delhi
The Seventh Session of the Eighteenth Lok Sabha, which commenced on 28 January, 2026, concluded today.
On this occasion, Shri Birla informed the House that 31 sittings were held during the Session which lasted for around 151 hours 42 minutes.
The productivity of the House during the Session was 93 percent, informed Shri Birla.
The  Hon’ble President of India addressed Members of both the Houses of Parliament on 28 January, 2026 and the discussion on Vote of Thanks on the President’s Address lasted for 2 hours 46 minutes, informed Shri Birla.
The Finance Minister presented Union Budget 2026-2027 on the floor of the House on 1 February, 2026. General Discussion on the Union Budget 2026-27 lasted for approximately 13 hours. Shri Birla informed that 63 Members participated in the discussion. Finance Minister replied to the discussion on 11 February, 2025.
Demands for Grants of selected Ministries/ Departments were discussed in the House from 16 to 18 March, 2026 and subsequently the Demands for Grants were passed by the House. Appropriation Bill was passed in the Lok Sabha on 18 March, 2026 and the Finance Bill was passed on 25 March, 2026.
Shri Birla further informed that, 12 Government Bills were introduced and 09 Bills were passed, during the session. Some of the important bills which were passed are as follows:
1. The Industrial Relations Code (Amendment) Bill, 2026
2. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026
3. Finance Bill, 2026
4. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2026
5. The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026
6. The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026
7. The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Bill, 2026
On this occasion, Shri Birla informed that the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-First Amendment) Bill, 2026; the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026; and the Delimitation Bill, 2026 were discussed in the House on 16 and 17 April, 2026 and the discussion lasted for 21 hours and 27 minutes. He also informed that 131 Members participated in the discussion on the three bills. The Constitution Amendment Bill was not passed by the House, he added.
Shri Birla also informed that on March 23, 2026, the Prime Minister delivered a statement regarding the ongoing conflict in West Asia and the challenges emerging before India.
During the Session, 126 starred questions were answered orally. A total of 326 Matters of Public Importance were raised by the Members during the Zero Hour, Shri Birla informed. A total of 650 matters were taken up under Rule 377 during the Session.
73 Reports were presented by Departmentally Related Standing Committees and as many as, 2089 papers were laid on the Table of the House, informed Shri Birla.
On 30 March 2026, a Short-Duration discussion was held under Rule 193 on the subject
“
Efforts to free the country from Left-Wing Extremism.” The discussion lasted for 6 hours and 7 minutes, and 36 Members participated in it. The discussion concluded with a reply by the Union Minister of Home Affairs.
Shri Birla also informed that on 16th April, 2026, the Chair informed the House of the significant achievement of India’s 500 MW Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor attaining first criticality successfully.
He also informed that during this session, 181 statements were made by Members in 18 Indian languages, and their simultaneous interpretation was carried out successfully.

Posted On:

Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha has appointed Dr. K. S. Somashekhar as Secretary in the Rajya Sabha Secretariat with effect from April 18, 2026. A 1993 entrant to the Secretariat, he has held several key positions, including Additional Secretary, Joint Secretary, and Director, with extensive experience in parliamentary interpretation, administration, and committee work. Dr. Somashekhar holds a Ph.D. in Literature and is proficient in Kannada, Hindi, English, Telugu and Tamil, bringing rich administrative and academic experience to his new role.

content:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
Text of the Valedictory remarks made in the House today by Hon'ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha
Posted On:
                        18 APR 2026 11:33AM by PIB Delhi
CHAIRMAN:
Hon'ble Members, with the conclusion of the 270th  Session of the Rajya Sabha, we mark the end of the Budget Session of Parliament. I am deeply appreciative of your valuable perspectives that enriched the discussions in the House.
Among the three sessions of the Parliament, the Budget Session holds the place of primacy. It is not only the longest of all three sessions but also the most consequential in shaping the nation’s growth trajectory. The budgetary allocations approved, the policies endorsed and the priorities affirmed during this Session have a direct bearing on the life of every citizen of Bharat.
Hon'ble Members, the Session commenced with the discussion on the Motion of Thanks to the Hon'ble President’s Address spanning over four days, during which 79 Members of this House participated with effusive energy and earnestness. The reply of the Hon'ble Prime Minister to the discussion on the Motion of Thanks brought clarity and context to the many points raised by the Hon'ble Members across the aisle.
The discussion on the Union Budget 2026–27 was equally incisive and comprehensive.  Spanning over four days, it witnessed the participation of as many as 97 Members. Besides, the House also held substantial discussions on the working of two key Ministries of the Government.
The House also took note of the suo moto statements made by the Minister of Commerce and Industry on India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement and the Minister of External Affairs regarding the situation in West Asia. The statement made by Hon'ble Prime Minister on the ongoing West Asia conflict and the challenges faced by India especially to meet its energy requirements as a result of it, presented the evolving situation in a proper perspective and underlined the need for a collective resolve of the nation to face it.
I am pleased to note that as many as 50 Private Members’ Bills were introduced during this Session.
I am delighted to share that on 94 occasions, Hon’ble Members spoke in 12 regional languages included in the 8th Schedule to the Constitution.
Overall, the House functioned for a total of 157 hours and 40 minutes. The productivity of this Session stood at 109.87 per cent. During the Session, we had the opportunity to raise 117 questions, 446 zero hour submissions and 207 special mentions.
Hon'ble Members, this Session also witnessed the re-election of Shri Harivansh ji as the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha for third time. The Hon’ble Prime Minister, along with Leaders and Members across the political spectrum, felicitated Shri Harivansh ji on his re-election.
I appreciate the cooperation extended by all in transacting the business of the House and extend my appreciation to the Hon'ble Deputy Chairman, Shri Harivansh ji and Members on the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons for assisting me in conducting the proceedings of the House.
I also thank the Leader of the House, the Leader of the Opposition, Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, the Leaders of various Parties and Groups and all Hon'ble Members for their kind cooperation extended by them.
I acknowledge the untiring efforts of the Secretary-General and his team of dedicated officers and staff in ensuring that the Session runs smoothly. I also thank the print and electronic media for covering the proceedings of the House and keeping the public informed.
Now, the National Song.
(The National Song "Vande Mataram" to be played)
CHAIRMAN
: The House stands adjourned sine die.

content:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the essence of people’s representative
PM greets public representatives across the country on the occasion of Panchayati Raj Day
Posted On:
                        24 APR 2026 10:20AM by PIB Delhi
The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the the essence of people’s representative:
“प्रजासुखे सुखं राज्ञः प्रजानां च हिते हितम्।
नात्मप्रियं प्रियं राज्ञः प्रजानां तु प्रियं प्रियम्॥"
The Subhashitam conveys, "The happiness of the people’s representative lies in the happiness of the people; his welfare lies in the welfare of the people. People’s representative has no personal favourites. Whatever is dear to the people is what is dear to him."
