title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality on Manoharpur to Dausa National Highway (in Rajasthan LSA)

questions.question:
With reference to the Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), consider the following statements:

1. The test assessed the real-time quality of mobile network services across 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks.
2. Performance parameters measured during the test include Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Jitter, and Packet Drop Rate.
3. The findings are primarily intended to inform consumers and encourage Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) to improve services.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.text: 1 and 2 only
answerOptions.rationale: While statements 1 and 2 are technically accurate regarding the scope and parameters, they do not encompass the full regulatory intent mentioned in the source.

answerOptions.text: 2 and 3 only
answerOptions.rationale: This selection omits the critical fact that the IDT methodology covers all generations of mobile technology from 2G to 5G.

answerOptions.text: 1 and 3 only
answerOptions.rationale: While 1 and 3 are correct, statement 2 is also a factual component of the Quality of Service (QoS) parameters assessed by TRAI.
The IDT is a comprehensive assessment covering all network generations, multiple QoS parameters (voice and data), and serves as both a consumer information tool and a TSP incentive.

questions.hint: Think about the multi-dimensional scope of the assessment, covering technology, technical metrics, and regulatory objectives.

questions.question: According to the TRAI findings for the Manoharpur to Dausa National Highway, which of the following is the prescribed threshold below which signal strength is classified as 'poor' for 4G and 5G technologies?

answerOptions.rationale: This value is actually the threshold defined for 2G technology in the report's methodology.
The report specifies this threshold for 3G technology, rather than the newer 4G or 5G standards.
This is a common intermediate signal value but is not the specific regulatory threshold cited for poor coverage in this IDT.
TRAI defines signal strength as poor for 4G and 5G if it falls below the $-110$ dBm level.

questions.hint: Consider the technical sensitivity requirements for modern high-speed data networks compared to legacy voice networks.

questions.question: Regarding the data performance of Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) on NH-148, identify the TSP that recorded the highest average download throughput and the one that recorded the highest average upload throughput respectively.

answerOptions.text: RJIL and RJIL
answerOptions.rationale: While RJIL led in download speeds, it did not hold the top spot for upload speeds according to the measured results.

answerOptions.text: RJIL and Airtel
answerOptions.rationale: RJIL achieved the highest download throughput at $247.01$ Mbps, while Airtel achieved the highest upload throughput at $20.93$ Mbps.

answerOptions.text: Airtel and RJIL
answerOptions.rationale: This reverses the leaders for download and upload; Airtel's download was significant but lower than RJIL's.

answerOptions.text: Airtel and VIL
answerOptions.rationale: VIL's upload performance was competitive at $17.25$ Mbps but was lower than the top-performing provider in that category.

questions.hint: One provider dominated the high-speed download metrics, but another was slightly more efficient in data transmission from the device to the network.

questions.question: Based on the TRAI report, which of the following statements regarding 'Call Silence Instances' is correct?

answerOptions.text: VIL recorded the highest number of call silence instances due to its 2G network fallback.
answerOptions.rationale: VIL actually recorded zero call silence instances, making it the best performer in this specific parameter.

answerOptions.text: Call silence was not checked for BSNL because its 4G coverage was unavailable on the test route.
answerOptions.rationale: The report explicitly mentions that since BSNL's 4G coverage was not available on the national highway, these instances could not be verified.

answerOptions.text: RJIL recorded fewer call silence instances than Airtel during the established calls.
answerOptions.rationale: RJIL recorded 3 instances, while Airtel recorded 2, meaning RJIL had more instances than Airtel.

answerOptions.text: Call silence is defined as any disruption in voice services lasting more than 10 seconds.
answerOptions.rationale: The report defines call silence instances as those observed for greater than 3 seconds.

questions.hint: Consider the technological limitations faced by the state-owned provider mentioned in the text.

questions.question:
Consider the following observations regarding the 'Coverage Gap' parameter for the TSPs on the Manoharpur to Dausa route:

1. RJIL recorded the lowest number of samples with poor signal strength.
2. Both Airtel and RJIL maintained zero samples with limited service (No Coverage).
3. BSNL recorded more samples with poor signal strength than all other TSPs combined.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.text: 1 and 2 only
answerOptions.rationale: While 1 and 2 are correct, the math for statement 3 must also be verified against the combined total of the other three providers.

answerOptions.text: 2 and 3 only
answerOptions.rationale: Statement 1 is a primary finding of the report and cannot be excluded from a correct assessment of the coverage gap.

answerOptions.text: 1 and 3 only
answerOptions.rationale: Statement 2 is a key factual point in the 'Annexure' table regarding limited service samples for the top private providers.
All statements are correct: RJIL had the fewest poor samples (189); Airtel/RJIL had 0 'No Coverage' samples; and BSNL's 2213 poor samples exceeded the sum of Airtel (217), RJIL (189), and VIL (420).

questions.hint: Perform a comparative calculation using the specific sample counts provided for each telecom service provider in the annexure.

title: Union Home Minister & Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah to chair 10th Apex-Level Meeting of NCORD on Friday, 26 June 2026 in New Delhi

questions.question:
Regarding the 10th Apex-Level Meeting of the Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) scheduled for June 2026, consider the following statements:

1. It is being organized by the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. The meeting involves participation from exactly 108 Central Ministries and Departments.
3. The meeting is conducted in a hybrid mode to include representatives from State Governments and Drug Law Enforcement Agencies.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.text: 1 and 3 only
answerOptions.rationale: The event is organized by the NCB and features a hybrid participation model for states, but the 108 figure refers to representatives from State Governments/DLEAs, while only 44 Central Ministries are involved.

answerOptions.text: 1 and 2 only
answerOptions.rationale: While the NCB is the organizer, the number of Central Ministries involved is 44, not 108, which is the count for state-level representatives.

answerOptions.text: 2 and 3 only
answerOptions.rationale: The participation count of 108 belongs to state and law enforcement agency representatives, making any statement pairing it with Central Ministries inaccurate.
This option is incorrect because statement 2 incorrectly attributes the number of state representatives to central ministries.

questions.hint: Distinguish between the number of participating Central Ministries and the number of representatives from State Governments.

questions.question: The 'Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029)' outlines a roadmap based on which primary pillars of drug control?

answerOptions.text: Demand-reduction, supply-reduction, and harm-reduction
answerOptions.rationale: The roadmap specifically identifies these three areas as the shared framework for addressing the drug menace over the next three years.

answerOptions.text: Incarceration, border sealing, and international litigation
answerOptions.rationale: While enforcement is part of the strategy, the document emphasizes a broader approach including rehabilitation and harm reduction rather than just punitive measures.

answerOptions.text: Supply-reduction, maritime security, and economic sanctions
answerOptions.rationale: These elements are too narrow and miss the critical demand and harm reduction aspects emphasized in the official vision.

answerOptions.text: Public awareness, crop destruction, and pharmacy regulation
answerOptions.rationale: These are specific tactics that fall under the broader pillars of demand and supply reduction rather than being the pillars themselves.

questions.hint: Consider the three-pronged approach common in comprehensive public health and safety frameworks.

questions.question: What is the specific target for the 'Online Drug Disposal Fortnight Campaign' to be launched by the Union Home Minister?

answerOptions.text: Destruction of approximately $2,09,500$ kg of narcotics valued at $\text{\u20b9}6,000$ crore
answerOptions.rationale: The campaign aims to facilitate the legal destruction of this specific quantity and value of seized drugs across the country.

answerOptions.text: Seizure of over $5,00,000$ kg of synthetic drugs from the darknet
answerOptions.rationale: The campaign focuses on the disposal (destruction) of already seized drugs rather than setting a new seizure target for the fortnight.

answerOptions.text: Destruction of $1,00,000$ kg of drugs worth $\text{\u20b9}10,000$ crore
answerOptions.rationale: This figures contradict the specific data provided in the release regarding the weight and estimated value.

answerOptions.text: Registration of $2,09,500$ new cases against traffickers within fifteen days
answerOptions.rationale: The 'Fortnight Campaign' is explicitly for drug disposal, not a drive for filing new legal cases.

questions.hint: The campaign focuses on the mass destruction of existing seized contraband.

questions.question: The 'Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029)' introduces a 'network-centric' enforcement approach. What is a key focus of this strategy according to the source material?

answerOptions.text: Addressing challenges of synthetic drugs and darknet-enabled trafficking
answerOptions.rationale: The document specifies that the roadmap envisages this approach to meet modern challenges like digital trafficking and synthetic narcotics.

answerOptions.text: Establishing a singular global database managed by the United Nations
answerOptions.rationale: The source focuses on national-level coordination and the integration of domestic agencies rather than an international database.

answerOptions.text: Focusing exclusively on the physical surveillance of land borders
answerOptions.rationale: Network-centric enforcement suggests a wider scope, including digital and inter-agency coordination, rather than just physical border security.

answerOptions.text: Replacing state law enforcement agencies with a single central task force
answerOptions.rationale: The document emphasizes inter-agency coordination and measurable targets for all stakeholders, not the abolition of state agencies.

questions.hint: Look for the modern, technology-driven threats mentioned in the roadmap.

questions.question: Which two locations will house the newly built NCB Zonal offices to be inaugurated during the meeting?

answerOptions.text: Jammu and Guwahati
answerOptions.rationale: The press release explicitly mentions the inauguration of zonal offices in these two specific cities.

answerOptions.text: Srinagar and Imphal
answerOptions.rationale: While these are sensitive regions for drug control, they are not the locations identified for the new offices in this announcement.

answerOptions.text: Jammu and Shillong
answerOptions.rationale: Jammu is correct, but the second location is Guwahati, which is the primary gateway in the Northeast mentioned in the text.

answerOptions.text: Leh and Guwahati
answerOptions.rationale: Guwahati is correct, but the other location is Jammu, not Leh.

questions.hint: Identify the two cities, one in the North and one in the Northeast, mentioned for institutional strengthening.

questions.question: The Vision Document (2026-2029) is designed to serve as a framework for which of the following?

answerOptions.text: Policy formulation, implementation, and institutional strengthening
answerOptions.rationale: The text states the document will be a guiding framework for these three specific areas to curb the drug menace.

answerOptions.text: Immediate decriminalization of personal drug consumption
answerOptions.rationale: The government’s stance is a 'Zero Tolerance Policy' against trafficking, and the document focuses on control and rehabilitation rather than decriminalization.

answerOptions.text: The privatization of rehabilitation and treatment centres
answerOptions.rationale: While it mentions expanding the reach of such centres, it does not suggest a policy of privatization; it emphasizes a 'whole-of-government' approach.

answerOptions.text: Direct federal control over state police narcotics divisions
answerOptions.rationale: The framework integrates and coordinates agencies but maintains the existing federal structure of enforcement.

questions.hint: The document covers the entire lifecycle of narcotics control policy from creation to execution.

questions.question: What is the stated underlying philosophy of the government's approach to drug trafficking, as emphasized by the Prime Minister?

answerOptions.text: Zero Tolerance Policy
answerOptions.rationale: The press release explicitly mentions that the meeting reinforces the 'Zero Tolerance Policy' as highlighted by PM Modi.

answerOptions.text: Harm Reduction First
answerOptions.rationale: While harm reduction is a pillar of the roadmap, the overarching government policy toward trafficking is described as 'Zero Tolerance'.

answerOptions.text: Soft Power and Persuasion
answerOptions.rationale: The government's approach to illegal trafficking involves strict enforcement and 'Zero Tolerance' rather than soft power strategies.

answerOptions.text: Community-Led Prohibition
answerOptions.rationale: While public awareness is mentioned, the core policy directive is the 'Zero Tolerance' stance against the traffickers themselves.

questions.hint: This phrase is commonly used to describe a strict, uncompromising stance against illegal activities.

questions.question: Which of the following documents is set to be released along with the Vision Document (2026-2029)?

answerOptions.text: NCB Annual Report- 2025
answerOptions.rationale: The release notes that the Union Home Minister will release both the new Vision Document and the NCB's annual report for the previous year.

answerOptions.text: National Survey on Substance Abuse 2026
answerOptions.rationale: The specific report mentioned is the NCB Annual Report for 2025, not a 2026 survey.

answerOptions.text: Darknet Trafficking Index 2024
answerOptions.rationale: While darknet trafficking is a challenge addressed in the Vision Document, no such index is mentioned for release.

answerOptions.text: State-wise Drug Control Rankings
answerOptions.rationale: The source material does not mention the release of any state rankings during this specific meeting.

questions.hint: It is an annual publication detailing the activities of the primary drug control agency.

questions.question: The 'whole-of-government' approach mentioned in the release primarily implies which of the following?

answerOptions.text: Coordinated action across all relevant central and state agencies and departments
answerOptions.rationale: The meeting brings together 44 Central Ministries and 108 state/agency representatives to ensure every part of the government works together against drugs.

answerOptions.text: The transfer of all drug-related legal powers to the Ministry of Home Affairs
answerOptions.rationale: A 'whole-of-government' approach implies coordination and shared responsibility, not the centralization of all powers into a single ministry.

answerOptions.text: Excluding non-governmental stakeholders from drug policy discussions
answerOptions.rationale: The release notes the Vision Document was prepared through consultations with various stakeholders, suggesting an inclusive rather than exclusive process.

answerOptions.text: The replacement of state laws with a singular federal drug code
answerOptions.rationale: The approach focuses on operational coordination and common goals (like the Vision Document) rather than legislative consolidation.

questions.hint: Think about how multiple layers and sectors of government collaborate on a single issue.

questions.question: Based on the Vision Document's roadmap, what specific social goal is prioritized to protect the future of the country?

answerOptions.text: Keeping youth away from drugs and expanding rehabilitation reach
answerOptions.rationale: The roadmap explicitly includes actions to keep youth away from drugs and improve treatment and rehab facilities.

answerOptions.text: Mandatory drug testing for all university students
answerOptions.rationale: The document focuses on 'keeping youth away' through prevention and awareness, rather than mentioning mandatory testing.

answerOptions.text: Lowering the legal age for tobacco and alcohol consumption
answerOptions.rationale: This contradicts the government's vision of a 'drug-free India' and the focus on reducing substance-related harm.

answerOptions.text: Banning all digital platforms that use encrypted communications
answerOptions.rationale: While it addresses darknet trafficking, it focuses on 'network-centric enforcement' rather than a blanket ban on encrypted platforms.

questions.hint: This involves a focus on the most vulnerable demographic and their recovery.

content:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister & Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah to chair 10th Apex-Level Meeting of NCORD on Friday, 26 June 2026 in New Delhi
Union Home Minister will also release the “Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029)” & “NCB Annual Report- 2025”
Vision Document will serve as a guiding framework for realizing PM Modi’s vision of a drug-free India
Shri Amit Shah will launch the Online Drug Disposal Fortnight Campaign to facilitate the destruction of 2,09,500 kg of drugs worth ₹6,000 crore
Shri Amit Shah will inaugurate NCB Zonal offices in Jammu & Guwahati
High Level meeting to review & assess collective national effort to combat Drug menace
Posted On:
                        24 JUN 2026 2:33PM by PIB Delhi
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah will chair the 10th Apex-Level Meeting of the Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) on Friday, 26 June 2026, at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The meeting, being organized by the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) will play a crucial role in further strengthening the government’s efforts to achieve PM Modi’s vision of a drug-free India. It will bring together key stakeholders from 44 Central Ministries and Departments, along with 108 representatives from State Governments and Drug Law Enforcement Agencies in hybrid mode.
On the occasion, Union Home Minister will release the “Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029). Prepared through wide-ranging consultations with concerned Central Government Departments, Drug Law Enforcement Agencies and other stakeholders, the Vision Document will provide a shared roadmap for addressing the demand-reduction, supply-reduction and harm-reduction aspects of the drug menace. The roadmap which envisages network centric enforcement approach, also includes the actions to be taken to meet the challenges of synthetic drugs, darknet-enabled trafficking, keeping youth away from drugs, expanding the reach of treatment and rehabilitation centres for drug users, among other measures in a coordinated and sustained manner over the next three years. This document clearly defines responsibilities, timelines and measurable targets for all stakeholders while integrating enforcement, demand reduction, rehabilitation, public awareness, capacity building, and inter-agency coordination. This Vision Document will serve as a guiding framework for policy formulation, implementation and institutional strengthening across the country to curb the menace of drugs.
Shri Amit Shah will also release NCB Annual Report- 2025 and inaugurate the newly built NCB Zonal offices in Jammu and Guwahati. The Drug Disposal Fortnight Campaign, a special drive to destroy narcotics. During the fortnight, approximately 2,09,500 kg of drugs worth ₹6,000 crore are expected to be destroyed across India, in accordance with the law, by various Central and State law-enforcement agencies.
The meeting will provide a platform for a comprehensive review and assessment of the collective efforts undertaken by all concerned stakeholders in combating the drug menace in the country. The deliberations will enable the participating States, departments and agencies to move forward with renewed vigour and commitment towards achieving the goal of effective narcotics control. While underscoring the need for a whole-of-government approach to effectively
combating
the drug menace in the country, the high-level meeting will deliberate on key issues relating to effectively combat drug trafficking & drug abuse across the country over the next three years.
This meeting is expected to reinforce the Government’s ‘Zero Tolerance Policy’ against drug trafficking in the country as emphasized by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

answerOptions.rationale: The ISP is a short-term indicator for the formal services sector's real output growth, mirroring the IIP's role for the industrial sector, but it specifically excludes the informal sector.

answerOptions.rationale: While the ISP is a counterpart to the IIP, it relies primarily on GST and administrative data, which inherently limits its coverage to the formal sector.

answerOptions.text: 1 and 3 only

Including the informal sector would require different high-frequency data sources not currently utilized for the ISP's primary monthly release.

answerOptions.rationale: Ms. Debjani Ghosh, a distinguished fellow at NITI Aayog, was appointed in May 2025 to lead the TAC in finalizing the ISP's methodological framework.

answerOptions.text: The Secretary of MoSPI
answerOptions.rationale: While MoSPI is the implementing ministry, the committee was specifically chaired by a distinguished fellow from NITI Aayog to ensure multi-disciplinary input.

answerOptions.text: The Chief Statistician of India
answerOptions.rationale: The chairperson was selected from NITI Aayog to bridge policy and statistical expertise, rather than being the head of the statistical office.

answerOptions.text: A representative from the Reserve Bank of India
answerOptions.rationale: The RBI is a stakeholder, but the leadership of this specific technical committee was designated to a fellow from the government's premier policy think tank.

questions.hint: The chairperson is associated with NITI Aayog, India's leading policy think tank.

questions.question:
Which of the following service sub-sectors are explicitly excluded from the current scope of the Index of Services Production (ISP)?

1. Public administration and Defence
2. Financial services excluding Banking and Insurance
3. Real estate activities
4. Gambling and betting activities

answerOptions.text: 1, 2, and 4 only
answerOptions.rationale: Public administration, non-banking financial services, and gambling are excluded because they are either non-market activities or dominated by the informal sector; real estate, however, is included.

answerOptions.text: 1 and 2 only
answerOptions.rationale: While these are excluded, the list also includes other activities like gambling and betting which do not fit the formal market output criteria for ISP.

answerOptions.text: 2, 3, and 4 only
answerOptions.rationale: Real estate is a covered sector under the ISP framework using GST data, making its inclusion in an exclusion list incorrect.
Real estate is actually one of the sectors targeted for inclusion using GST-based value indicators.

questions.hint: Identify which of these are typically considered 'non-market' or 'core government' activities versus commercial services.

questions.question: How does MoSPI plan to incorporate the Health and Education sub-sectors into the ISP, given they are largely exempt from GST?

answerOptions.text: By using results from the Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises (ASISSE)
answerOptions.rationale: Since GST data is unavailable for these exempt sectors, MoSPI intends to use ASISSE survey data to estimate their contribution to the ISP.

answerOptions.text: By using proxy data from the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Education
answerOptions.rationale: While administrative data is used for some sectors, the ISP specifically targets the 'incorporated' or formal private portion of health and education via ASISSE.

answerOptions.text: By applying the growth rates of the Transport and Communication sectors as a proxy
answerOptions.rationale: The ISP methodology seeks specific indicators for each sector rather than relying on unrelated sectoral proxies for major categories like education.

answerOptions.text: By using voluntary disclosures from private hospitals and universities
answerOptions.rationale: Statistical indicators require systematic data collection like surveys or administrative records rather than irregular voluntary disclosures.

questions.hint: Look for the specific survey mentioned as a data source for sectors where GST data is not applicable.

questions.question: In the methodology of the ISP, why is 'turnover' considered a suitable indicator for measuring service production?

answerOptions.text: Services are generally consumed as they are produced, meaning turnover closely reflects production without inventory lag.
answerOptions.rationale: Unlike manufacturing, services cannot be easily stored, so the value of sales (turnover) is a near-perfect proxy for the volume of production at any given time.

answerOptions.text: Turnover is the only variable captured by the Service Accounting Codes (SAC) under GST.
answerOptions.rationale: While SAC helps classify services, the suitability of turnover is based on the economic nature of services (perishability) rather than just the classification system.

answerOptions.text: It eliminates the need for price deflators during the calculation of real growth.
answerOptions.rationale: Turnover is a nominal value and actually necessitates the use of deflators to convert it into a volume-based (real) measure.

answerOptions.text: Turnover accounts for both formal and informal sector transactions equally.
answerOptions.rationale: Turnover data in the ISP is derived from GST, which specifically filters for the formal, registered sector.

questions.hint: Think about the unique characteristics of services compared to physical goods, specifically regarding storage and timing.

questions.question: The Index of Services Production (ISP) uses different deflators to convert nominal values into real volume. Which deflator is proposed for the Banking and Insurance sub-sectors?

answerOptions.text: CPI General
answerOptions.rationale: Aligned with the recommendations for the GDP base year revision, the General Consumer Price Index is used as a proxy deflator for financial sub-sectors.

answerOptions.text: WPI (Wholesale Price Index)
answerOptions.rationale: WPI is specifically used for Wholesale Trade, but is not considered appropriate for financial services like banking.

answerOptions.text: CPI (Non-Food)
answerOptions.rationale: CPI Non-Food is used for many other service sectors where specific indices are missing, but Banking and Insurance have been assigned CPI General.

answerOptions.text: Service Producer Price Index (SPPI)
answerOptions.rationale: Although SPPIs are available for some sectors, they are quarterly and lagged, making them less feasible for the monthly ISP compared to CPI.

questions.hint: This choice is based on methodological improvements suggested for the base year revision of GDP.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the proposed base year and the expected lag for the regular release of the ISP indices?

answerOptions.text: Base Year 2024-25; Lag of 60 days
answerOptions.rationale: The 2024-25 base year was chosen for its recency and alignment with the new CPI series, with indices released monthly after a 60-day window.

answerOptions.text: Base Year 2011-12; Lag of 45 days
answerOptions.rationale: The 2011-12 base is used for older indices; the ISP is a modern indicator utilizing the most recent possible base period.

answerOptions.text: Base Year 2024-25; Lag of 30 days
answerOptions.rationale: While the base year is correct, the complexity of aggregating GST and administrative data requires a slightly longer lag of 60 days.

answerOptions.text: Base Year 2022-23; Lag of 90 days
answerOptions.rationale: The base year is tied specifically to the 2024 CPI update, and a 90-day lag would be too long for a high-frequency indicator.

questions.hint: The base year aligns with the most recent Consumer Price Index (CPI) series update mentioned in the text.

questions.question: According to the source material, why is the CPI (Non-Food) index considered an acceptable general deflator for services in the absence of specific indices?

answerOptions.text: Non-food items include housing and transport, which are significant cost-push factors for service producer prices.
answerOptions.rationale: Over $80\%$ of non-food inflation is linked to services or their inputs (like energy and housing), making it a stable proxy for service sector price movements.

answerOptions.text: The non-food category accounts for nearly $90\%$ of the total weight of the overall CPI.
answerOptions.rationale: The text states non-food items account for nearly $63\%$ of the total weight, not $90\%$.

answerOptions.text: Food prices are generally more stable than service prices, which would distort the index.
answerOptions.rationale: Actually, food prices are noted as less stable, which is why they are excluded from this specific deflator to ensure the proxy is reliable.

answerOptions.text: It is the only index that accounts for Service Accounting Codes (SAC).
answerOptions.rationale: SAC is a classification system for taxes and mapping, not a price index or deflator itself.

questions.hint: Focus on the relationship between non-food components like 'Housing' and 'Transport' and the operational costs of service providers.

questions.question: For which of the following sub-sectors does the ISP use quantity-based indicators rather than value-based indicators?

answerOptions.text: Air Transport and Railways
answerOptions.rationale: These sectors allow for direct measurement of output in physical terms, such as passenger-kilometers, removing the immediate need for price deflation.

answerOptions.text: Banking and Insurance
answerOptions.rationale: These financial sectors rely on value-based indicators that must be deflated by the CPI General.

answerOptions.text: Telecommunications and Postal services
answerOptions.rationale: Telecom uses turnover deflated by CPI (communications), making it a value-based indicator in the ISP framework.

answerOptions.text: Wholesale and Retail Trade
answerOptions.rationale: Trade output is measured via outward supplies (value) and deflated by WPI or other price indices.

questions.hint: Think of sectors where output is commonly measured in units like 'kilometers travelled' rather than 'rupees earned'.

questions.question: What is the primary function of Service Accounting Codes (SAC) in the compilation of the ISP?

answerOptions.text: They facilitate the mapping of GST outward supplies to the National Industrial Classification (NIC) codes.
answerOptions.rationale: SACs provide the product-level detail necessary to group GST data into the industry-level categories used in the ISP's sectoral indices.

answerOptions.text: They serve as the primary price deflator for the real output calculation.
answerOptions.rationale: SAC is a classification scheme, not a price index; deflators like CPI or WPI are used for the actual calculation.

answerOptions.text: They provide the weights based on Gross Value Added (GVA).
answerOptions.rationale: Weights are derived from National Account Statistics, while SAC is used to organize the incoming high-frequency data.

answerOptions.text: They determine the eligibility of a service for GST exemption.
answerOptions.rationale: While used in the GST system, the SAC's role in the ISP context is purely for statistical mapping and aggregation.

questions.hint: SAC acts as a bridge between the taxation system's labels and the statistical system's industrial categories.

content:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
FAQs on Index of Services Production – Trial Indices with Base year 2024 -25
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                        24 JUN 2026 2:29PM by PIB Delhi
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) is preparing to launch Index of Services Production (ISP) in July, 2026, which shall be a new macro indicator to measure the short-term changes in the growth of the services sector. As counterpart of the IIP which measures the economic growth of the industrial sector, ISP will cover the formal services sector and will be released on a monthly basis.
To assist MoSPI in the finalization of the conceptual & methodological framework for compiling ISP, a Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) on compilation of ISP, was constituted in May, 2025, under the chairpersonship of Ms. Debjani Ghosh, distinguished fellow, NITI Aayog. Apart from representatives from academia and the Industry associations, the TAC – ISP has members from the Ministries / departments of the services sector.
Based on the deliberations held in the TAC, MoSPI brought out an Approach paper comprising of detailed methodological approach and framework for compilation of ISP on 27
th
April, 2026, which was placed in the public domain for seeking comments and suggestions of various stakeholders.
The Report of the TAC – ISP will be released in first fortnight of July, 2026, which will inter-alia cover the scope and coverage, conceptual & methodological framework for compilation of ISP in alignment with the international best practices.
MoSPI envisages to release an overall ISP alongwith sub – sectoral indices on a trial basis. The sectoral coverage of ISP includes sub sectors like wholesale and retail trade, transport, banking, insurance, telecommunications, hotels & restaurants, real estate, professional, scientific and technical services, arts, entertainment & recreation, etc. Two sub – sectors, namely, Health and education services are proposed to be brought into the ISP framework later, after the results of Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises (ASISSE) are released.
The base year of ISP is selected as 2024 -25. The trial monthly indices for the year 2025 -26 and for the month of April, 2026 are slated for release on 14
th
July, 2026. Thereafter, regular release of the monthly trial indices will be made with a lag of about 60 days on the 29
th
Day (or next working day in case of a holiday) of every month.
To assist users and other stakeholders in appreciating the methodological & conceptual framework of compilation of ISP series, MoSPI is releasing, through this press release, a booklet on Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).
***
FAQs on Index of Services Production
What is the Index of Services Production (ISP)?
The Index of Services Production (ISP) is a short-term indicator designed to measure changes over time in the volume of output produced by the services sector relative to a specified base period. It measures changes in the real output of service-producing industries over time.
What is the contribution of services sector in the Indian economy and why is an ISP needed?
The services sector has emerged as the dominant force in the Indian economy, contributing over 50% of the Gross Value Added since 2013-14. Considering its growing importance and potential, and inline with global practices, India needs a short-term indicator to measure the growth of services sector to enable planners and policymakers to take suitable measures & guide its growth trajectory.
3.         What are the objectives of ISP?
The two main aims for compiling ISP are to provide:
Economic trends that would complement an IIP on the short – term movement of an economy; and
High frequency information on the performance of the services sector to strengthen the existing statistical framework to support analytical and policy framework.
What are the benefits of ISP?
ISP will provide timely information on the performance of services industries, thereby, strengthening monitoring of economic activity and supporting evidence-based policy decisions. In addition, ISP will serve as a high-frequency indicator of services sector growth and will provide timeseries data to enable better economic forecasting and business cycle analysis. Main users of ISP would be National Accounts, economic Ministries / departments, domain experts and researchers.
What were the major challenges that India was not able to compile an ISP earlier?
The compilation of an ISP requires high-frequency, reliable and representative indicators of service sector output. Unlike manufacturing, where production can often be measured through physical quantities of goods produced, services are largely intangible and many service activities do not have directly observable output measures. Historically, compilation of ISP in India faced several challenges, including:
Limited availability of administrative datasets covering service-producing industries;
Heterogeneous nature of service activities requiring sector-specific output indicators;
Non-availability of suitable service sector price indices for deriving volume measures;
Consequently, the compilation of a comprehensive high-frequency ISP was not feasible.
What developments have made the compilation of ISP feasible now?
Over the last decade, significant improvements have taken place in India's statistical and administrative data ecosystem, making compilation of ISP feasible. These developments primary include availability of high-frequency GST data on outward supplies of service-producing units; Commencement of the Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises (ASISSE) will provide periodic data for compilation of ISPs of sub – sectors like Health and Education which are not possible to cover through GST data.
Why are experimental / trial indices being released and when will the regular indices be released?
MoSPI will utilize three main data sources for ISP namely administrative data, GST and ASISSE. As some of these sources are still evolving and GST data will be used for the first time in statistical applications, trial or experimental ISP indices will be released for some time to observe their stability and resilience. Thereafter, regular compilation and dissemination will take place.
What are the major data sources proposed for ISP?
The three principal data sources are:
· Administrative/secondary data for ISP of Air Transport, Railway Transport, Banking and Insurance;
· GST data for Wholesale Trade, Retail Trade, Repair and Maintenance, Accommodation and Food, Road Transport, Water Transport, Warehousing and support activities for transportation, Postal & courier, Telecommunications, Information and Broadcasting, Real estate, Information and computer related services, Professional, scientific & technical services including R & D, Administrative & support services and Arts, Entertainment & Recreation, etc.;
· Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises (ASISSE) data for Health and Education (excluding Government) sectors.
Will ISP cover the informal services sector?
No. ISP will primarily reflect the formal sector as it is compiled using outward supply of enterprises registered under GST.
Is the entire services sector covered in ISP?
Some of the services which are not covered in ISP are those which are either related to core government activities or are dominated by non – market activities and the informal sector. The excluded services sub-sectors are:
Public administration and Defence
Financial services excluding Banking and Insurance (e.g. activities of the Central Bank, Money Market Funds)
Social work activities without accommodation
Services of membership organisations
Personal services
Activities of private households with employed persons
Activities of extraterritorial organisations
Health and Education services provided by Government and
Gambling and betting activities
How are Health and Education sub – sectors, exempt from GST will be covered in ISP?
Indices of Health and Education sub – sectors (excluding government contribution) are planned to be compiled on the basis of estimates from ASISSE surveys.
What will be the frequency of release of All India ISP?
ISP will be released with a monthly frequency with a lag of about 60 days.
What are quantity-based indicators?
Quantity based indicators directly measure the output in physical quantities terms such as passenger-kilometers travelled in case of Air Transport. In ISP, indices of only two sub – sectors, namely, Air Transport and Railways are based on quantity output.
What are value-based indicators?
Indicators where output is measured in value terms such as revenue, sales or outward supplies are the value-based indicators.
What are the preferred indicator variables for measuring service output?
Considering the International guidelines and deliberations in the TAC, the preferred and alternate indicators for each sector/sub-sector were identified considering Indian situation. Generally, the preferred indicator is turnover deflated by an appropriate price index, where available.
Why turnover is considered a suitable output indicator?
Considering that services are consumed as soon as they are produced and generally do not involve inventory accumulation; therefore, turnover closely reflects production.
What are the Service Accounting Codes (SAC)?
The Service Accounting Code (SAC) is the Scheme of Classification under the Indian Goods and Services Tax (GST) system. It is a modified version of the United Nations Central Product Classification (CPC), with modifications adapted for the Indian context by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC). SAC is used to classify different types of services for the purposes of taxation, invoicing, and filing GST returns. SACs facilitate mapping of GST outward supplies to the National Industrial Classification (NIC) codes of the services industries.
How are GST data transformed into output measures?
Aggregated data on SAC wise Taxable Value of Sales (outward supplies), as obtained from the return GSTR 1, can be considered as the output variable in value terms. GSTN has made available product / service wise (SAC codes) data on ‘outward supplies’ for different service activities as extracted from monthly GST returns.  MoSPI does not have access to nor does it require individual unit level data for this purpose.
The production of services directly results into its sale / consumption. Hence, use of GST data of outward supplies essentially reflects production of services. Outward supplies of SACs mapped to a particular NIC code are aggregated and then deflated to obtain real output measures.
What is a deflator?
The ISP tracks short-term changes in the
volume
of services produced. Because primary service data is usually collected in value terms (nominal value), it captures the effects of both the prices and value addition. A price deflator is therefore required to remove the effects of change in prices from nominal service revenue. It transforms "value-based" (nominal) data into "volume-based" (real) data, allowing measurement of actual changes in service output over time.
What deflators are used in ISP?
Following deflators are used,
· WPI for Wholesale trade;
· Sector-specific CPI, wherever available;
· CPI General for Banking and Insurance
· CPI Non-Food, elsewhere;
What are international guidelines on deflators for ISP?
As per International Practice, the Service Producer Price Indices (SPPIs) are preferred as deflators for ISP, in case of non-availability of SPPI, CPI is recommended.
Why has SPPI not been used for ISP?
The data on SPPI is available only for limited services. In respect of the sub – sectors being covered under ISP; SPPIs are available only for five sub- sectors, namely, Air Transport, Railways, Telecom, Banking and Insurance for which SPPI were available. In case of Air Transport and Railways, as the output indicator of ISP is in terms of quantity, no deflator is required.
Further, as the SPPIs are available with a quarterly frequency and lag of 60 days their use in monthly ISP may not be feasible. Thus, use of CPI (communications) as a deflator for telecom sub – sector will be made. In case of financial sub – sectors (Banking and Insurance), in accordance with the report of the sub – committee on ‘Methodological improvement for the base year revision of GDP (base year 2022 -23), use of general CPI as a deflator for sub- sectors will be made.
Why CPI is considered an acceptable proxy?
For many services, producer and consumer prices move closely because services are consumed soon after production. The use of CPI in absence of SPPIs is acceptable considering that services are consumed as soon as they are produced, thus, SPPIs and CPIs differ only by tax margin at one level (level of consumer). Considering the taxes are constant, there may not be any significant differences between the two.
In the absence of both SPPI and sub – sector specific CPI, why has use of CPI (Non – food) been proposed as a general deflator.
This proposition finds merit in the logic that inflation of services moves in tandem with inflation of non-food items (which are generally more stable than food items) in view of the following:
The non – food items account for nearly 63% of the total weight of overall CPI. The non – food items include items of services also, which account for nearly 28% of the total weight of overall CPI and nearly 44.44% of the non- food weight.
Another significant division in the non – food items category is "Housing, Water, Electricity, Gas and Other Fuels", this accounts for nearly 17.67% of the total weight of the overall CPI and 28% weight in the non - food category. 'Housing, Water, Electricity, Gas and Other Fuels' are significant contributors to inflation in services. They act as major cost-push factors by either directly driving up operating expenses for businesses & producer prices or increasing the cost of living for employees leading to higher wage demands & in turn higher producer prices.
Other significant cost push factor items in the non – food category include petrol, diesel and CNG which are under the Transport Division of CPI which account for nearly 4.85% of the total weight of the overall CPI and 7.7% weight in the non -food category.
Thus, in all more than 80% of the Non – food inflation is attributable either directly to services or its cost push factors.
What is the proposed base year for ISP?
The proposed base year of trial ISPs is 2024 -25 which meets both the recency and normal year criteria. The choice of base year considers the fact that for most of the sub – sectors, CPI based deflators are proposed to be used. As the base of the new series of CPI is 2024, it was felt that 2024 -25 may be more appropriate a choice for the base year.
How are weights assigned in ISP?
Weights are based on sectoral contributions to Gross Value Added (GVA) available from National Account Statistics.
Why are GVA-based weights used?
They reflect the relative economic importance of each services industry.
What is the proposed compilation formula?
ISP is proposed to be compiled using a fixed-weight Laspeyres volume index.
Click here to see pdf

Samrat
(रिलीज़ आईडी: 2277392)

title: Discussion Paper on Methodological Approaches for Compilation of Monetary Asset Accounts of Coal in India

questions.question:
Regarding the SEEA Central Framework followed by MoSPI for natural resource accounting, consider the following statements:

I. It is an international statistical standard endorsed by the United Nations Statistical Commission.
II. It primarily focuses on the monetary valuation of environmental assets, excluding physical asset accounts.
III. It provides a conceptual framework for measuring the economic value embodied in a nation's natural resource endowment.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

answerOptions.text: I and III only
answerOptions.rationale: The SEEA is indeed a UN-endorsed standard that covers both physical and monetary accounts to measure economic value in natural endowments.

answerOptions.text: I and II only
answerOptions.rationale: While Statement I is correct, the SEEA framework includes both physical and monetary accounts rather than excluding physical ones.

answerOptions.text: II and III only
answerOptions.rationale: The framework's inclusion of physical accounts contradicts Statement II, though Statement III correctly identifies the purpose of monetary valuation.

answerOptions.text: I, II, and III
answerOptions.rationale: Statement II is incorrect because physical asset accounts are a foundational component of the SEEA framework used by MoSPI since 2018.

questions.hint: Evaluate whether environmental accounting standards typically ignore the physical quantity of resources.

questions.question: Which specific methodology has been identified as the most appropriate for the Indian context for compiling monetary asset accounts of coal, and what is its primary valuation approach?

answerOptions.text: OECD (2025) using the Net Present Value (NPV) approach
answerOptions.rationale: The Discussion Paper identifies the OECD methodology as superior due to its alignment with SNA 2025 and its use of the NPV approach via the Residual Value Method.

answerOptions.text: World Bank (CWON 2024) using the Market Exchange Value approach
answerOptions.rationale: While the World Bank methodology was reviewed, it was not selected as the primary approach for India's national statistical system.

answerOptions.text: Philippines-based methodology (2024) using the Replacement Cost method
answerOptions.rationale: The Philippines methodology was one of the three reviewed alternatives but was not deemed the most appropriate for India's data infrastructure.

answerOptions.text: SNA (2025) using the Direct Market Price observation method
answerOptions.rationale: SNA 2025 is a system of accounts that the OECD methodology aligns with, but the specific approach recommended is NPV through resource rents.

questions.hint: Consider which international organization’s guide is grounded in the latest System of National Accounts.

questions.question: The 'Residual Value Method' mentioned in the Discussion Paper is utilized to estimate which of the following components?

answerOptions.text: Future resource rents
answerOptions.rationale: The Residual Value Method is applied within the NPV approach to estimate resource rents by drawing on national accounts aggregates.

answerOptions.text: Historical extraction costs
answerOptions.rationale: While extraction costs are part of the calculation, the method's ultimate goal is to isolate the rent or surplus value of the resource itself.

answerOptions.text: Social cost of carbon
answerOptions.rationale: The Discussion Paper focuses on economic asset valuation rather than the negative externalities or social costs associated with carbon emissions.

answerOptions.text: Total proven geological reserves
answerOptions.rationale: Reserves are part of physical accounts; the Residual Value Method is a monetary tool for financial valuation.

questions.hint: Think about the economic term for the surplus value generated by a natural resource after accounting for all production costs.

questions.question: Based on the PIB release, what was the recorded production level for raw coal and lignite respectively in India for the period 2024-25?

answerOptions.text: $1,047.523$ million tonnes and $45.133$ million tonnes
answerOptions.rationale: These specific figures are cited in the paper to underscore the strategic importance of coal and lignite to India's energy security.

answerOptions.text: $1,047.523$ million tonnes and $145.133$ million tonnes
answerOptions.rationale: The figure for raw coal is correct, but the lignite production is significantly over-represented in this option.

answerOptions.text: $845.133$ million tonnes and $45.133$ million tonnes
answerOptions.rationale: The lignite figure is correct, but the raw coal production is under-represented compared to the record highs mentioned in the text.

answerOptions.text: $1,200.000$ million tonnes and $100.000$ million tonnes
answerOptions.rationale: These are rounded figures that do not match the precise record production data provided by the Ministry.

questions.hint: Look for the specific values associated with India's record-breaking production year for both fuel types.

questions.question: Which Indian policy framework specifically mandates sustainable mining practices, making the monetary valuation of coal resources directly relevant for policy implementation?

answerOptions.text: National Mineral Policy, 2019
answerOptions.rationale: The Discussion Paper explicitly links the need for monetary valuation to the mandates for sustainable mining found in the National Mineral Policy, 2019.

answerOptions.text: National Energy Policy, 2024
answerOptions.rationale: While energy policy is relevant to coal, the text specifically identifies the 2019 Mineral Policy as the driver for sustainable mining valuation.

answerOptions.text: Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan, 2020
answerOptions.rationale: The vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat is mentioned as a broader goal, but it is not the specific policy cited as mandating sustainable mining practices.

answerOptions.text: Environment Protection Act, 1986
answerOptions.rationale: This act is a general environmental law; the text points to a more recent and specific mineral-focused policy from 2019.

questions.hint: Focus on the specific sectoral policy mentioned that governs the extraction and management of minerals.

questions.question: Which combination of data sources is primarily used for compiling the physical asset accounts for coal in India as presented in the Discussion Paper?

answerOptions.text: Geological Survey of India, EnviStats India, and Energy Statistics India
answerOptions.rationale: The paper specifies that physical accounts for 2015-16 to 2023-24 used data from the GSI through the EnviStats and Energy Statistics series.

answerOptions.text: Ministry of Coal, Central Electricity Authority, and NITI Aayog
answerOptions.rationale: While these bodies deal with coal, the text explicitly cites the GSI and MoSPI's own statistical publications as the primary sources.

answerOptions.text: Indian Bureau of Mines, National Sample Survey, and World Bank
answerOptions.rationale: The Indian Bureau of Mines is involved in minerals, but the document highlights the GSI and EnviStats as the specific sources for the paper's data.

answerOptions.text: Directorate General of Mines Safety and National Accounts Statistics
answerOptions.rationale: National Accounts Statistics are used for monetary valuation, but the physical accounts rely on geological and energy-specific data series.

questions.hint: The sources include a geological body and two statistical series published by MoSPI.

questions.question: Why is the OECD (2025) methodology considered more feasible within India's existing statistical infrastructure compared to other international models?

answerOptions.text: Its reliance on National Accounts Statistics (NAS) compiled by MoSPI
answerOptions.rationale: The OECD approach is favored because its data requirements align well with the NAS aggregates already produced by India's national statistical system.

answerOptions.text: Its use of satellite imagery and real-time mining sensors
answerOptions.rationale: The text emphasizes conceptual rigour and national accounts aggregates rather than high-tech physical monitoring tools.

answerOptions.text: Its simplicity in excluding capital consumption and taxes from resource rent
answerOptions.rationale: The methodology is described as conceptually rigorous, implying it handles complex economic variables rather than simplifying them through exclusion.

answerOptions.text: Its exclusive focus on private sector profitability rather than government revenue
answerOptions.rationale: The valuation supports the estimation of future government revenues, suggesting it is not limited to private sector data.

questions.hint: Look for the connection between the chosen methodology and the data MoSPI already collects regularly.

questions.question: In the context of the SEEA framework, what is the primary benefit of transitioning from physical asset accounts to monetary asset accounts?

answerOptions.text: Enabling comparison across different types of environmental assets and assessment of depletion costs
answerOptions.rationale: Monetary valuation provides a common metric (currency) that allows for the comparison of diverse resources and the calculation of economic loss due to depletion.

answerOptions.text: Replacing the need for physical data collection with financial estimates
answerOptions.rationale: Monetary accounts build upon physical accounts rather than replacing them; both are necessary for a complete picture.

answerOptions.text: Eliminating the reliance on international statistical standards like the SNA
answerOptions.rationale: The monetary accounts are actually designed to be more closely integrated with the System of National Accounts (SNA).

answerOptions.text: Focusing exclusively on renewable energy resources to meet climate goals
answerOptions.rationale: The current paper specifically addresses coal, a non-renewable resource, to improve its sustainable management.

questions.hint: Consider why putting a price tag on different resources (like coal vs. water) might help a policymaker compare them.

questions.question: Since which year has the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) been compiling physical asset accounts for coal and other mineral resources?

answerOptions.rationale: MoSPI began following the UN SEEA Framework for compiling physical asset accounts in 2018, providing the foundation for current monetary efforts.
While the physical accounts in the paper cover the period from 2015-16, the systematic adoption of the UN SEEA framework by MoSPI started in 2018.
2024 is the year associated with some of the data publications and methodology reviews, but the process started much earlier.
2026 is the current date of the Discussion Paper release, representing an advanced stage of the project rather than its inception.

questions.hint: The text mentions a specific year as the starting point for following the UN SEEA Framework.

content:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Discussion Paper on Methodological Approaches for Compilation of Monetary Asset Accounts of Coal in India
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                        24 JUN 2026 1:11PM by PIB Delhi
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has released a Discussion Paper titled "
Methodological Approaches for Compilation of Monetary Asset Accounts of Coal in India
", aligned with the
System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) Central Framework
, endorsed by the United Nations Statistical Commission as an international statistical standard.
Since 2018, MoSPI has been following the UN SEEA Framework and compiling physical asset accounts for coal and other mineral and energy resources through the
EnviStats India series
and
Energy Statistics India
. Building on this foundation, MoSPI has taken a further step by initiating the experimental monetary valuation and compilation of monetary asset accounts for mineral and energy resources.
The monetary valuation of environmental assets provides a measure of the economic value embodied in India's natural resource endowment, enables assessment of depletion costs, supports the estimation of future government revenues from resource extraction, and facilitates comparison across different environmental assets. The National Mineral Policy, 2019 mandates sustainable mining practices, making such valuation directly relevant to India's policy framework.
About the Discussion Paper
The Discussion Paper presents a detailed conceptual framework for monetary valuation of non-renewable mineral and energy resources as prescribed in the SEEA Central Framework, and systematically reviews and compares three alternative international methodologies, OECD (2025) Compilation Guide for Measuring Natural Resources in the National Accounts, the World Bank's Changing Wealth of Nations (CWON, 2024), and the Philippines-based methodology (2024), examining their conceptual foundations, data requirements, and potential data sources for the Indian context to identify the most appropriate approach for adoption within India's national statistical system. The paper also presents physical asset accounts for coal in India for the period 2015-16 to 2023-24, using data from the Geological Survey of India through EnviStats India 2024 and Energy Statistics India 2025.
Coal has been selected as the illustrative case given its strategic importance to India's economy. As the nation's most abundant domestic energy resource, coal accounts for the majority of India's electricity generation and supports a wide range of core industries including steel, cement, and chemicals. India achieved record raw coal production of 1,047.523 million tonnes and lignite production of 45.133 million tonnes in 2024-25, underscoring the resource's centrality to India's energy security and the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision. At the same time, as a non-renewable resource, the need for its sustainable management makes monetary asset valuation all the more important.
Key Findings and Recommended Methodology
Of the three methodologies reviewed, the OECD (2025) methodology is identified as the most appropriate for the Indian context, given its conceptual rigour, grounding in the SEEA Central Framework and the System of National Accounts (SNA 2025), and feasibility within India's existing data infrastructure, particularly the National Accounts Statistics (NAS) compiled by MoSPI. The methodology applies the Net Present Value (NPV) approach to future resource rents estimated through the Residual Value Method, drawing on national accounts aggregates.
This Discussion Paper is issued as an open invitation for comments and feedback from experts, researchers, government agencies, and international organisations. Responses received will assist in  finalisation of a standardised methodology for monetary valuation of non-renewable mineral resources within India's national accounts framework, placing India at the forefront of natural capital accounting among emerging economies. Accurate and transparent monetary valuation of India's mineral and energy resources will serve as a foundational input for data-driven policymaking and sustainable development.
Feedback may be submitted to the Environment Unit, Social Statistics Division, MoSPI at
ssd-mospi[at]gov[dot]in
.
The Discussion paper is available at the Ministry’s website
www.mospi.gov.in
Scan the QR code to access the Discussion Paper
***

content:
Ministry of Steel
PM Modi's Viksit Bharat Vision to Be Powered by a Digitally Transformed Steel Sector: H.D. Kumaraswamy
Digitalization No Longer a Choice, But Steel Sector's Survival Strategy: H.D. Kumaraswamy
Steel Sector Must Move Beyond Capacity Expansion to Intelligent Manufacturing: H.D. Kumaraswamy
"India's Steel Future Will Be Shaped by Data, AI and Smart Factories": H.D. Kumaraswamy
Chintan Shivir 2026 Charts Digital Transformation Path for India's Steel Industry
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                        24 JUN 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi
Union Minister for Steel and Heavy Industries H.D. Kumaraswamy on Wednesday asserted that digitalisation is no longer an option but the "foundational cornerstone of long-term survival" for India's steel industry, underscoring the need for the sector to embrace emerging technologies to remain globally competitive.
Addressing the Chintan Shivir 2026 on Digitalisation in the Steel Sector at Vigyan Bhawan in New Delhi, Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy said the future of the steel industry would not be determined merely by production capacities, but by its ability to build intelligent, connected and data-driven manufacturing ecosystems. Invoking Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047, H.D. Kumaraswamy described the steel sector as a strategic pillar of India's economic transformation, powering infrastructure creation, manufacturing, renewable energy, urbanisation, transportation and defence production.
"Steel is the backbone of nation-building," he said, noting that India has consistently retained its position as the world's second-largest steel producer since 2018, even as steel demand remains subdued in several advanced economies. Highlighting the sector's robust growth trajectory, the Minister pointed out that crude steel production has expanded at an average annual rate of nearly 8 percent since FY 2021-22, while finished steel consumption has grown by approximately 13 percent annually, reflecting strong domestic demand and rapid industrialisation.
Kumaraswamy reiterated the government's long-term vision of increasing India's steelmaking capacity to 300 million tonnes by 2030 and 400 million tonnes by 2035. However, he cautioned that achieving these targets would require the industry to simultaneously address challenges related to raw material security, operational efficiency, decarbonisation, modernisation and export competitiveness. Emphasising the transformative potential of technology, the Minister said Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Industrial Internet of Things, Digital Twins, Robotics and Advanced Data Analytics are redefining steel manufacturing globally and must be adopted extensively in India.
He observed that digitalisation and automation can significantly improve productivity, optimise energy consumption, reduce operational costs and enable predictive maintenance systems capable of identifying equipment failures before they occur. Such interventions, he said, would help minimise unplanned downtime, reduce human errors and enhance workplace safety.
The Chintan Shivir featured thematic sessions on AI-led mining solutions, digital transformation of steel plants, PM Gati Shakti, Industry 4.0 applications and case studies showcasing measurable business impacts. Leading startups and industry stakeholders also participated in discussions aimed at accelerating the sector's technological transition. Expressing confidence in the deliberations, Kumaraswamy said the insights emerging from the forum would contribute towards building a smarter, greener, more efficient and globally competitive steel industry aligned with the Prime Minister's vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047.
Held under the Ministry of Steel, the conclave brought together senior officials of the Ministry, along with Chairmen and Managing Directors of major steel public sector undertakings, including SAIL, NMDC and MOIL, besides industry leaders, startups and technology experts.
***
AG
(रिलीज़ आईडी: 2277384)

content:
NITI Aayog
Six Youth-Led Sustainability Startups Win Youth Co:Lab National Innovation Challenge 2026
Top innovators in circular economy, sustainable textiles, and food systems honoured at T-Hub, Hyderabad; selected from more than 350 applicants across 28 states
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                        24 JUN 2026 11:21AM by PIB Delhi
Six youth-led startups from across India have been recognized as winners of the 8th edition of the Youth Co:Lab National Innovation Challenge 2026 for developing innovative solutions that advance sustainability through circular economy innovations, sustainable textiles and fashion, and sustainable food systems and water conservation.
Co-led by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) India and Citi Foundation, in partnership with Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), and implemented by T-Hub Foundation, the Youth Co:Lab National Innovation Challenge has emerged as one of India's foremost platforms for empowering youth-led innovation that accelerates progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
This year, the challenge received over 350 applications from youth-led startups across 28 states. Following a rigorous selection process, 50 high-potential startups were enrolled in the National Springboard Programme, a three-month virtual capacity-building journey supported by a curated group of 16 industry mentors and domain specialists.
The participating startups worked across three thematic areas:
• Sustainable Textiles and Fashion
• Circular Economy Innovations
• Sustainable Food Systems and Water Conservation
All 50 startups pitched before a distinguished jury during the National Innovation Dialogue held on 4th June 2026. Following the evaluation, the top 20 startups advanced to the Regional Immersion Bootcamp hosted at T-Hub, Hyderabad from 15th to 19th June 2026.
The five-day immersive programme brought together ecosystem leaders, sustainability experts, investors, government stakeholders and entrepreneurs through masterclasses, mentorship sessions, site visits and peer learning opportunities designed to strengthen business models and scale impact.
Following a final jury evaluation on 18 June 2026, six startups were selected for their scalable, high-impact solutions.
The three winning startups received seed grant support of ₹3,50,000 each, along with capacity-building opportunities and ecosystem access. The three runners-up were awarded ₹2,20,000 each in recognition of their promising contributions and potential for scale.
Winners: NavaPrayoga Labs LLP (Grassip), UnBubble and Ecorenowa Solutions Pvt. Ltd.
Runners Up: Eco Cushion, Vasudeva Innovations and WomenasticCO
The awards were presented in the presence of senior representatives from UNDP, AIM, T-Hub, government institutions, investors and innovation ecosystem leaders.
Delivering the special address on
Building India's Green Economy: Youth, Capital and the Next Decade of Innovation
,
Meraj Faheem, CEO, Telangana Innovation Cell (TGIC), Government of Telangana
, said, "
Initiatives like Youth Co:Lab reinforces the power of innovation, collaboration, and youth leadership in addressing some of our most pressing challenges. We are proud to have been part of this journey and remain committed to nurturing ecosystems that enable young changemakers to transform ideas into meaningful impact
."
“India does not have a startup problem. India has a distribution problem. A distribution of capital — too concentrated in Bangalore and Delhi. A distribution of mentorship — too thin in Tier-3 and the North-East. A distribution of opportunity — too narrow for women, persons with disabilities, and founders from socially disadvantaged backgrounds. Programmes like Youth Co:Lab exist to fix that distribution problem. And the evidence we are unveiling today suggests they are starting to,” said Prateek Deshmukh, Program Director, Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog.
“One of India's greatest resources is its youth dividend. With nearly 65 percent of the population under the age of 35, the country's ability to meet its development and climate goals will depend on how effectively we support young innovators to turn ideas into action. More than 350 startups stepped forward with solutions to some of the most pressing challenges of our time, from waste and water scarcity to unsustainable production systems. # National Prosperity Through Collective Action: Analysis of the Prime Minister’s Sanskrit Subhashitam

## Executive Summary
On June 24, 2026, the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, issued a public communication centered on a Sanskrit *Subhashitam* (aphorism) to articulate a vision for national development. The core message emphasizes that the prosperity of a nation is not a static achievement but a dynamic result of collective dedication, enthusiasm, and the strategic combination of policy and valor. The Prime Minister's message frames these traditional values as the essential energy required to fulfill modern developmental resolutions and ensure the steadfast growth of society.

## Analysis of Key Themes

The communication highlights three primary pillars necessary for a thriving nation:

### 1. The Synergy of "Naya" and "Vikrama"
The Sanskrit verse shared by the Prime Minister emphasizes a specific combination for success:
*   **Policy (Naya):** The strategic and ethical framework of governance and action.
*   **Valor/Action (Vikrama):** The courage and physical effort required to implement goals.
The text posits that when policy and valor are united (*samyoga*), prosperity (*Shri*) becomes "achala" (immovable) and "dhruvam" (certain).

### 2. Collective Dedication and Effort
The Prime Minister translates the ancient wisdom into a contemporary socio-political context, focusing on:
*   **Samuhik Samarpan (Collective Dedication):** The idea that progress is not the responsibility of a few but requires the total commitment of the entire society.
*   **Purushartha (Human Endeavor):** The emphasis on hard work and diligent effort as the foundation of national wealth.

### 3. Eradication of Inertia
A central theme in the *Subhashitam* is the prerequisite of **Alasya-vihinata** (the absence of laziness). The Prime Minister suggests that by removing inertia and replacing it with an "enthusiastic beginning" (*utsaha-samarambho*), society gains the "new energy" needed to bridge the gap between setting resolutions and achieving success.

---

## Key Quote and Contextual Analysis

### The Sanskrit Subhashitam
> "यत्रोत्साहसमारम्भो यत्रालस्यविहीनता।
> नयविक्रमसंयोगस्तत्र श्रीरचला ध्रुवम्॥"

**Context:** Shared via the Prime Minister's official X (formerly Twitter) account and disseminated through the Press Information Bureau (PIB). This verse serves as the philosophical foundation for the government's message on national progress.

### The Prime Minister's Interpretation
> "Collective dedication and effort keep the prosperity of the nation intact. It is this very spirit that infuses society with new energy and paves the way to fulfill the resolutions of development."

**Analysis:** This statement serves as a bridge between classical Indian philosophy and modern governance. It identifies "spirit" and "energy" as the drivers of "resolutions" (Sankalp), suggesting that economic or material development is a byproduct of the underlying character and collective will of the people.

---

## Elements of National Prosperity
Based on the text provided, the following table breaks down the essential components required for a nation to remain prosperous:

| Component | Definition in Context | Impact on the Nation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Utsaha** | Enthusiasm and proactive initiation. | Infuses society with new energy. |
| **Alasya-vihinata** | Lack of laziness/Inertia. | Ensures continuous movement toward goals. |
| **Naya** | Policy, strategy, and justice. | Provides the direction for growth. |
| **Vikrama** | Valor, bravery, and effort. | Provides the power to execute the strategy. |
| **Samuhik Samarpan** | Collective dedication. | Keeps national prosperity "achala" (steadfast). |

---

## Actionable Insights for National Development

The principles outlined in the Prime Minister's message suggest a multi-pronged approach to achieving developmental "resolutions":

*   **Foster Collective Ownership:** Development must be framed as a collective endeavor (*Samuhik*) rather than a top-down mandate to ensure the "prosperity of the nation remains steadfast."
*   **Integrate Strategy with Implementation:** Success depends on the "combination of policy and valor." Leaders and citizens must ensure that well-crafted policies are backed by the courageous effort to see them through.
*   **Maintain Momentum:** By emphasizing the "enthusiastic beginning" and the "absence of laziness," the text suggests that maintaining momentum is critical to reaching the "perfection of resolutions."
*   **Cultivate Social Energy:** The "spirit" of dedication is identified as a source of "new energy." Cultivating this spirit within the social fabric is essential for long-term national endurance.

title: Ambassador Jamieson Greer Leads U.S. Delegation to India for Bilateral Trade Agreement Talks
content:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Ambassador Jamieson Greer Leads U.S. Delegation to India for Bilateral Trade Agreement Talks

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUN 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi

United States Trade Representative Ambassador Jamieson Greer visited New Delhi from 22–24 June 2026, leading an official U.S. delegation. The visit marked a key step in ongoing efforts to advance a balanced, mutually beneficial India–U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) and to finalize an interim deal in line with the joint statement of 7 February 2026.

Ambassador Greer held multiple rounds of discussions with the Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal. The two leaders conducted a comprehensive review of core BTA elements, including enhanced market access, digital trade, supply chain resilience, reduction of non-tariff barriers, and expanded cooperation in strategic sectors.

Both sides noted substantial progress by negotiating teams in recent months and welcomed the momentum from successive technical and ministerial-level engagements. Discussions focused on pathways to conclude an interim agreement as an important milestone toward a comprehensive BTA. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to an agreement that is balanced, commercially meaningful, and delivers tangible benefits for businesses, farmers, workers, and consumers in both countries.

Recognizing the growing significance of the India–U.S. economic partnership amid evolving global trade dynamics, both sides reiterated their shared goal of expanding bilateral trade, fostering innovation, and building resilient, trusted supply chains.

The two sides expressed confidence that ongoing negotiations will further deepen economic ties and strengthen the India–U.S. Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.
